title: Announcing the Death of William McKinley
summary: Announced the death of President William McKinley and named Thursday, September 19, 1901, the day of his burial, a national day of mourning and prayer.

title: Fort Sill Military Reservation, Comanche County, Oklahoma Territory, enlarged by 893.07 acres, for the purpose of locating thereon certain Apache prisoners of war.
summary: Enlarged the Fort Sill Military Reservation in Comanche County, Oklahoma Territory, by 893.07 acres so certain Apache prisoners of war could be located there.

title: Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve, Colo., diminished, and described lands restored to the public domain.
summary: Shrank a Colorado forest reserve (printed as Black Mesa, but the lands lie in the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve) and returned the described lands to the public domain.

title: T. S. Sharretts appointed special appraiser of duties on imports into China.
summary: Named T. S. Sharretts special appraiser of duties on imports into China.

title: Ratings and pay of petty officers and other enlisted men of the Commissary Branch of the U.S. Navy established.
summary: Set the ratings and pay of petty officers and other enlisted men in the Navy's Commissary Branch.

title: Harbor Island and three islets southeast thereof in Sitka Harbor, Alaska, reserved for the use of the Revenue Cutter Service.
summary: Reserved Harbor Island and three islets southeast of it in Sitka Harbor, Alaska, for the Revenue Cutter Service.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Clerk in Pension Agency in Philadelphia Without Examination
summary: Let the vacancy for the clerk who signs checks for the pension agent at the Philadelphia pension agency be filled without a civil-service examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Steward in White House Without Examination
summary: Allowed the vacant post of White House steward to be filled without a civil-service examination.

title: Thanksgiving Day, 1901
summary: Set apart Thursday, November 28, 1901, as a day of national thanksgiving, while noting the country still mourned President McKinley.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Coachman in Navy Department Without Examination
summary: Allowed the Navy Department to fill a vacant laborer job, with the duties of coachman in the Assistant Secretary of the Navy's office, without a civil-service examination.

title: Certain lands in Zambales and Bataan, Island of Luzon, P. I., reserved for naval purposes.
summary: Reserved certain lands in Zambales and Bataan, on the island of Luzon in the Philippines, for naval purposes.

title: Certain described lands near Point Dume, Calif., reserved for lighthouse purposes, subject to any legal existing rights.
summary: Set aside described lands near Point Dume, California, for a lighthouse, subject to any legal existing rights.

title: Certain described lands in Arizona Territory adjoining the Moqui and Navajo Reservations withdrawn from sale pending homestead settlement by Indians residing thereon.
summary: Withdrew described lands in Arizona Territory next to the Moqui and Navajo reservations from sale, holding them until the Indians living there could settle them as homesteads.

title: San Nicolas Island, Calif., reserved for lighthouse purposes.
summary: Reserved San Nicolas Island, off California, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Certain United States Army Positions Subject to Classification
summary: Amended Civil Service Rule III by striking four clauses, (g) through (j), from its list of exceptions, bringing certain U.S. Army positions under classification.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Permitting Superintendents of Indian Training Schools to be Classified
summary: Changed the civil-service rules so that when an Indian training school superintendent took over an agency's duties, the displaced Indian agent could be made a classified employee after a fitness test.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Waiver of Apportionment Provisions for Transfers
summary: Amended the civil-service transfer rule so apportionment limits "may" (rather than "shall") be waived, and only with a detailed certificate approved by the Civil Service Commission.

title: Enlisted Navy men allowed additional monthly pay for good conduct.
summary: Granted enlisted men of the Navy extra monthly pay for good conduct.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Classification of Post Office Personnel
summary: Redefined the classified Post-Office Service to cover employees of free-delivery post offices and rural free delivery, with rural carriers held outside classification until their appointment regulations took effect.

title: Enlisted Navy men holding petty officers' training certificates allowed additional pay.
summary: Gave Navy enlisted men who held petty officers' training certificates additional pay.

title: Classification and monthly pay of Navy mess attendants authorized.
summary: Authorized a classification and monthly pay scale for Navy mess attendants.

title: Prescribing Procedure for Dismissal of Persons in Violation of Civil Service Act or Rules
summary: Set a procedure for removing people holding jobs in violation of the civil-service law: after notice, the Commission certifies the violation, and pay stops if the person isn't dismissed within thirty days.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Providing that Public Officers Cooperate with Civil Service Commission Investigations
summary: Required every federal officer and employee to give the Civil Service Commission information and sworn testimony in its investigations.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Prohibit Transfer of Persons Who Have not Served Six Months in Classified Position
summary: Barred transfers of civil servants who had not served at least six months in the office where they became classified.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Provide for Appointment from Incomplete Registers
summary: Let appointing officers hire from a register holding only one or two eligible candidates, as if a full list of three had been certified.

title: Certain described lands on Culebra Island, off Puerto Rico, placed under Navy Department jurisdiction, subject to existing private rights.
summary: Placed described lands on Culebra Island, off Puerto Rico, under the jurisdiction of the Navy Department, subject to existing private rights.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Age Limitations in Post Office Service
summary: Set separate civil-service age limits for rural letter carriers, ages 17 to 55, while keeping 18 to 45 for all other Post-Office positions.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Age Limitations in Post Office Service for War Veterans
summary: Waived the age limits for honorably discharged Civil War and Spanish-American War soldiers and sailors applying to be rural letter carriers.

title: Honorably discharged Civil War veterans, if fit and qualified, given preference in appointment and retention in government jobs.
summary: Gave honorably discharged Civil War veterans, if fit and qualified, preference in being hired and kept in government jobs.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Assistant Commissioner of Immigrations in New York Without Examination
summary: Allowed the vacant post of Assistant Commissioner of Immigration at the Port of New York to be filled without examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Exceptions from Examination for Draftsmen in Navy Department
summary: Amended the civil-service rules on which Navy Department draftsmen are excepted from examination.

title: Oklahoma City Land District, Oklahoma Territory, diminished by transfer of certain described lands to the El Reno and Mangum Land Districts.
summary: Shrank the Oklahoma City Land District in Oklahoma Territory, moving described lands into the El Reno and Mangum land districts.

title: Perry Land District and Land Office, Oklahoma Territory, abolished, and lands, records and business transferred to the Guthrie Land District and Land Office.
summary: Abolished the Perry Land District and land office in Oklahoma Territory and moved its lands, records and business to the Guthrie office.

title: Enid Land District and Land Office, Oklahoma Territory, abolished, and lands, records and business transferred to the Kingfisher Land District and Land Office.
summary: Closed the Enid Land District and land office in Oklahoma Territory, handing its lands, records and business to the Kingfisher office.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Age Limitations in Coast and Geodetic Survey
summary: Added civil-service age limits for watch officers (21 to 36) and chief engineers (25 to 45) in the Coast and Geodetic Survey.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Four Interior Department Special Inspectors from Examination
summary: Excepted four special inspectors in the Interior Department from civil-service examination, alongside the one special land inspector already excepted.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Remove Provision Allowing Reinstatement After Dismissal
summary: Struck the civil-service provision that let people dismissed for misconduct be reinstated beyond the one-year limit if the charges proved untrue.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Prohibit Transfers Except to Positions in Same Class
summary: Limited civil-service transfers to positions requiring the same class of work or the same mechanical trade as the employee's current job.

title: Requiring that Lists of All Positions Deemed Unclassified be Submitted to Civil Service Commission
summary: Ordered appointing officers in Washington's executive departments to give the Civil Service Commission detailed lists of every position treated as unclassified, so the Commission could decide each one's status.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Temporary Appointments
summary: Rewrote the rules for emergency and temporary appointments, limiting emergency hires to thirty days a year and requiring them to be reported to the Civil Service Commission.

title: Designating Reception Committee for Prince Henry of Prussia
summary: Named a reception committee for the visit of Prince Henry of Prussia.

title: Suitable reception and entertainment of Prince Henry of Prussia, while sojourning in the United States, ordered.
Soliciting Increase in Pay or Influencing Legislation by Employees of the United States
summary: Forbade federal executive employees, alone or through associations, from seeking pay raises or lobbying Congress in their own interest except through their department heads, on penalty of dismissal.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Allowing Transfers of Certain Personnel in Treasury Department
summary: Let certain Bureau of Engraving and Printing workers transfer without examination to money-counting and sorting jobs elsewhere in the Treasury, with limited later rights.

title: John P. Green, Classified as Postage Stamp Agent Without Examination or Certification in Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed John P. Green of Ohio, postage-stamp agent in the Post-Office Department since 1897, to be treated as holding a competitive position without examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except from Classification Certain Marine Hospital Service Personnel
summary: Updated the list of quarantine stations whose Marine-Hospital Service attendants are excepted from classification, and added temporary acting assistant surgeons and sanitary inspectors during epidemics.

title: Office of the Surveyor-General, Arizona Territory, transferred from Tucson to Phoenix.
summary: Moved the Office of the Surveyor-General of Arizona Territory from Tucson to Phoenix.

title: Albert H. Clark, injured in line of duty, made eligible for appointment as an assistant messenger in the War Department office.
summary: Made Albert H. Clark, injured in the line of duty, eligible for appointment as an assistant messenger in the War Department.

title: Amending Consular Regulations of 1896, Paragraph 692, Regarding Currency Certificates
summary: Revised the consular regulations on currency certificates for import invoices, letting a friendly nation's consul or two respectable merchants issue the certificate when they certify the invoice.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Require Examination Before Transfer from Positions which Became Classified
summary: Required people whose jobs became classified to pass the entrance examination before transferring to another department, office or branch.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Transfer After Reinstatement
summary: Barred reinstated federal employees from transferring until they had served six months in the office where they were reinstated.

title: Civil Service Commissioners' recommendation of Mar. 7, 1902 — that the entrance-examination age limit of twenty years under Rule V be suspended for Richard D. Micou and other applicants who passed the computer examination for the Naval Observatory and Nautical Almanac Office — approved.
summary: Approved the Civil Service Commission's recommendation to suspend the twenty-year age limit for Richard D. Micou and others who passed the computer exam for the Naval Observatory and Nautical Almanac Office.

title: Amending Consular Regulations Regarding Appointments to Office from Foreign States
summary: Barred consular officers from accepting appointment by a foreign state as administrator, guardian or other estate fiduciary without prior approval from the Secretary of State.

title: Office building and 200-ft-square tract in the abandoned Fort Yuma Military Reservation, Yuma County, Arizona Territory, reserved for the Weather Bureau.
summary: Reserved an office building and a 200-foot-square tract in the abandoned Fort Yuma Military Reservation, Arizona Territory, for the Weather Bureau.

title: Under the act of Feb. 14, 1902 (32 Stat. L. 20), Juneau Land District (entire Territory of Alaska), Land Office at Juneau, established and opened June 2, 1902; Circle, Sitka and Yukon Land Districts and their offices at Rampart City, Sitka and St. Michael discontinued May 31, 1902.
summary: Created a single Juneau Land District covering all of Alaska, opening June 2, 1902, and closed the Circle, Sitka and Yukon land districts and their offices on May 31.

title: Establishing the San Isabel Forest Reserve
countersigned_by: David J. Hill, Acting Secretary of State
summary: Created the San Isabel Forest Reserve in Colorado, setting the described timbered public lands apart from entry and settlement.

title: Establishing the Santa Rita Forest Reserve
summary: Established the Santa Rita Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, closing the described timbered public lands to entry and settlement.

title: Manila Bay Military Reservations (Mariveles, Calumpan Point, and islands and rocks between the two), Bataan and Cavite Provinces, P. I., ~180 sq. mi., established.
summary: Established the Manila Bay Military Reservations in the Philippines, about 180 square miles at Mariveles, Calumpan Point and the islands and rocks between them in Bataan and Cavite provinces.

title: Establishing the San Francisco Mountains Forest Reserve
summary: Consolidated the San Francisco Mountains Forest Reserves in Arizona Territory into a single reserve and added adjacent timbered lands to it.

title: Establishing the Niobrara Forest Reserve
summary: Set apart the Niobrara Forest Reserve in Nebraska, reserving the described public lands from entry and settlement.

title: Establishing the Dismal River Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Dismal River Forest Reserve in Nebraska from described public lands, closing them to entry and settlement.

title: Forbidding Criticisms of Diplomatic and Consular Service Officers by Others in Either Service Unless Confidential
summary: Forbade diplomatic and consular officers from publicly attacking or criticizing one another; any charges had to go confidentially to the State Department.

title: Flags ordered displayed at half-mast on all Federal buildings for the late J. Sterling Morton, former Agriculture Secretary.
summary: Ordered flags at half-mast on all federal buildings for the late J. Sterling Morton, former Secretary of Agriculture.

title: Residence building and described tract in the abandoned Fort Yuma Military Reservation, Yuma County, Arizona Territory, reserved for the Customs Service.
summary: Reserved a residence building and described tract in the abandoned Fort Yuma Military Reservation, Arizona Territory, for the Customs Service.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Exceptions from Examination for Certain Workers in Navy Department
summary: Placed Navy special mechanics, civilian inspectors and draftsmen under Navy Department labor regulations, with appointments made on navy-yard fitness tests instead of civil-service examinations.

title: Certain described lands near Point Dume, Calif., reserved for lighthouse purposes, subject to any legal existing rights.
summary: Reserved described lands near Point Dume, California, for lighthouse purposes, subject to any legal existing rights.

title: William B. Dunlany appointed messenger in the office of the Secretary to the President without examination, because of "peculiar qualifications."
summary: Appointed William B. Dunlany messenger in the office of the Secretary to the President without examination, citing his "peculiar qualifications."

title: Diminution of the Fort Hall Indian Reservation for Homesteads
summary: Opened to settlement the lands of the Fort Hall Indian Reservation in Idaho that the Shoshone and Bannock Indians had ceded to the United States under an agreement ratified in 1900.

title: Spanish-American War veterans in Government service in the District of Columbia excused from duty May 21 to attend the dedication of the statue to the Spanish-American War dead at Arlington Cemetery.
summary: Excused Spanish-American War veterans in federal jobs in the District of Columbia from duty on May 21 to attend the dedication of the statue to the war's dead at Arlington Cemetery.

title: Civil War veterans in Government service in the District of Columbia excused from duty May 17 to attend the reburial of the late W. S. Rosecrans, Major-General, U.S. Army.
summary: Gave Civil War veterans in federal jobs in the District of Columbia the day off on May 17 to attend the reburial of Major General W. S. Rosecrans.

title: Establishment of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve and the Teton Forest Reserve
summary: Replaced the Yellowstone Park Timber Land Reserve and the earlier Teton Forest Reserve in Wyoming with newly bounded Yellowstone and Teton forest reserves.

title: Establishing the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve
summary: Established the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve in Wyoming, closing the described timbered public lands to entry and settlement.

title: Enlargement of the Big Horn Forest Reserve
summary: Enlarged the Big Horn Forest Reserve in Wyoming, adding described townships and reserving them from entry or settlement.

title: Flags ordered displayed at half-mast on all Federal buildings for the late Lord Pauncefote, British Ambassador.
summary: Ordered flags at half-mast on all federal buildings in honor of the late Lord Pauncefote, the British Ambassador.

title: Restoring to the Public Domain Certain Lands in the State of California
summary: Restored Section 7, Township 15 South, Range 2 East, San Bernardino Meridian, California, to the public domain, removing it from lands once reserved for the Captain Grande band of Mission Indians.

title: Declaration of the Meaning of Section 8, Rule II, of the Civil Service Rules
summary: Defined "just cause" for removal from the classified civil service as any cause, other than a merely political or religious one, that promotes the efficiency of the service.

title: Lot 1 of block 40, Alva, Oklahoma Territory, reserved for post office purposes.
summary: Reserved Lot 1 of Block 40 in Alva, Oklahoma Territory, for post office purposes.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Assistant Commissioner of Immigration in New York Without Examination
summary: Allowed the vacancy for Assistant Commissioner of Immigration at the port of New York to be filled without a civil-service examination.

title: Coal Depot, Amaknak Island, Alaska, established on certain lands reserved for lighthouse purposes by Executive Order of Jan. 13, 1899.
summary: Established a coal depot on Amaknak Island, Alaska, on lands reserved for lighthouse purposes in 1899.

title: Enlargement of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve
summary: Added described lands in Wyoming to the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, reserving them from entry or settlement.

title: San Felipe Pueblo Indian Reservation, New Mexico Territory, established for the use and occupation of the Indians of the Pueblo of San Felipe, subject to valid existing rights (lapsed rights to be added to the reservation).
summary: Established the San Felipe Pueblo Indian Reservation in New Mexico Territory for the Indians of the Pueblo of San Felipe, subject to valid existing rights.

title: Boundary line between the WaKeeney and Colby, Kans., Land Districts altered and redescribed.
summary: Redrew the boundary between the WaKeeney and Colby land districts in Kansas.

title: Certain described lands in Kitsap County, Wash., reserved for the use of the Navy Department as a target range.
summary: Reserved described lands in Kitsap County, Washington, for a Navy target range.

title: Certain lands on Adak and Kiska Islands, Alaska, reserved for naval purposes.
summary: Reserved certain lands on Adak and Kiska islands, Alaska, for naval purposes.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Alexander C. Caine as Disbursing Clerk in Justice Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let the Justice Department fill its vacant disbursing-clerk job by transferring Alexander C. Caine from his excepted post as examiner, without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Restoring to the Public Domain Certain Lands in the Territory of Oklahoma
summary: Returned 38.6 acres once reserved for the Kiowa and Comanche Indian Agency to the public domain, so the adjoining city of Anadarko, Oklahoma Territory, could acquire it for a park.

title: Establishment of the White River Forest Reserve
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the White River Plateau Timber Land Reserve in Colorado and renamed it the White River Forest Reserve.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Certain Aliens Qualify for Copperplate Map Engraver Position
summary: Opened the copperplate map engraver examination to foreign-born applicants who had declared their intention to become U.S. citizens, to supply enough eligibles.

title: Louisiana Purchase Exposition
summary: Formally proclaimed the new schedule for the Louisiana Purchase Exposition in St. Louis: buildings dedicated by April 30, 1903, and opening to visitors no later than May 1, 1904.

title: Establishing the Santa Catalina Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Santa Catalina Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, setting the described timbered public lands apart from entry and settlement.

title: Suspending Duties on Cuban Vessels Entering Ports of the United States
summary: Suspended discriminating tonnage and import duties on Cuban vessels and their cargoes in U.S. ports, for as long as Cuba exempted American vessels from such duties.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Recommendations for Promotion
summary: Ruled that only an employee's supervisors may recommend promotions; outside recommendations made with the employee's knowledge could bar the promotion, and a repeat could mean removal.

title: Prescribing Manner for Appointment of Unclassified Laborers in Executive Departments and Independent Officers
summary: Ordered that unclassified laborers in executive departments and independent offices be hired under regulations approved by department heads and the Civil Service Commission.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Allow Transfer of Certain Former Employees in the Military Government in Cuba
summary: Allowed certain former employees of the U.S. military government in Cuba, commended for service amid danger from yellow fever and other tropical diseases, to be appointed in the classified service.

title: Granting Pardon and Amnesty to Participants in Insurrection in the Philippines
summary: Granted full pardon and amnesty to people in the Philippines who took part in, or aided, the insurrections against Spain and the United States, with exceptions and excluding the Moro country.

title: Regulations governing discharge of Navy enlisted men before completion of term established.
summary: Established regulations for discharging Navy enlisted men before the end of their terms.

title: Modifying the Boundary Lines of the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve
summary: Redrew the boundary lines of the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve in Wyoming, set out the new limits, and fixed a date when lands left outside the reserve would open to settlement.

title: Permitting Issuance of Passports to Residents of Insular Possessions of United States
summary: Changed passport rules so U.S. diplomats and consuls could issue passports to residents of the nation's insular possessions who swore allegiance to the United States and backed their application with two credible witnesses.

title: Rules Governing the Granting and Issuing of Passports in the United States
summary: Laid out the rules for getting a U.S. passport at home: only the Secretary of State issues them, applicants must owe allegiance to the United States, and applications take the form of a sworn affidavit with a personal description.

title: Rules Governing the Granting and Issuing of Passports in the Insular Possessions of the United States
summary: Set the rules for issuing passports in the insular possessions, directing applicants to the chief executive of each possession and requiring a sworn affidavit from anyone owing allegiance to the United States.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Clerk in New York Immigration Office from Examination
summary: Amended Civil Service Rule VI so one confidential clerk to the commissioner of immigration at the port of New York could be hired without examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Lawyer in New York Immigration Office from Examination
summary: Amended Civil Service Rule VI to exempt one immigrant inspector and law clerk in the New York immigration commissioner's office from examination.

title: Establishment of the Mount Graham Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Mount Graham Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, describing its boundaries and closing the land to settlement.

title: Miraflores Island in San Juan Harbor, P. R., reserved as site for quarantine station or marine hospital under the Public Health and Marine Hospital Service.
summary: Reserved Miraflores Island in San Juan Harbor, Puerto Rico, as a site for a quarantine station or marine hospital run by the Public Health and Marine Hospital Service.

title: Ellen W. Fitzsimmons made eligible for transfer from the abolished office of Commissioner of Railroads to the Post Office Department without regard to Civil Service Rule X, section 11.
summary: Made Ellen W. Fitzsimmons eligible to move from the abolished office of Commissioner of Railroads to the Post Office Department, waiving a civil-service transfer rule.

title: Compulsory retirement of Revenue Cutter Service officers reaching age sixty-four ordered.
summary: Ordered compulsory retirement for Revenue Cutter Service officers once they reached age sixty-four.

title: Establishment of the Lincoln Forest Reserve
summary: Established the Lincoln Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, setting its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.

title: Establishment of the Chiricahua Forest Reserve
summary: Set apart the Chiricahua Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, describing its limits and closing the land to settlement.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except War Department Clerk in White House Duty from Examination
summary: Allowed a $1,000-a-year War Department clerk, to be detailed for duty at the White House, to be appointed without civil-service examination.

title: Appointment of a clerk, War Department, at $1,000 per annum for duty at the White House, without examination, authorized.
Seamen Gunners or enlisted men holding certificates from petty officers' schools, seaman gunner class, allowed two dollars per month additional pay.
summary: Gave seamen gunners, and enlisted men holding certificates from the seaman gunner class of the petty officers' schools, two dollars a month in extra pay.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Solicitor at Port of New York from Examination
summary: Amended Civil Service Rule VI so the collector at the port of New York could have one solicitor appointed without examination.

title: Ratification of Creek Indians-U.S. Treaty
summary: Proclaimed that the supplemental agreement between the United States and the Muskogee (Creek) Nation, approved by Congress and by the Creek national council, was ratified and had the force of law.

title: Certain described lands in Nebraska reserved for the Agriculture Department for experimental tree planting.
summary: Reserved described lands in Nebraska for the Department of Agriculture to use for experimental tree planting.

title: John T. Heck made eligible for reinstatement in the Government Printing Office without regard to length of separation from the service.
summary: Made John T. Heck eligible for reinstatement in the Government Printing Office no matter how long he had been out of the service.

title: Regulations governing the discharge of Navy enlisted men established.
summary: Set regulations governing the discharge of enlisted men from the Navy.

title: Establishment of the Little Belt Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Little Belt Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, defining its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.

title: Establishment of the Madison Forest Reserve
summary: Established the Madison Forest Reserve in Montana, laying out its boundaries and closing the land to settlement.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except from Classification Temporary Marine Hospital Service Personnel
summary: Widened a civil-service exception so Marine-Hospital Service workers hired temporarily to keep contagious diseases from entering or spreading, in the United States or elsewhere, needed no examination.

title: Establishment of the Alexander Archipelago Forest Reserve
summary: Reserved Chichagof, Kupreanof, Kuiu, Zarembo and Prince of Wales islands and neighboring islands in Alaska as the Alexander Archipelago Forest Reserve, while protecting valid rights held under the 1867 treaty with Russia.

title: Restoring Fort Sill Indian Sub-Agency Lands to the City of Lawton, Oklahoma for Cemetery
summary: Returned 40 acres once held for the Fort Sill Indian sub-agency to the public domain so the nearby city of Lawton, Oklahoma Territory, could acquire it for a cemetery.

title: Establishment of the Absaroka Forest Reserve
summary: Established the Absaroka Forest Reserve in Montana, describing its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.

title: Directing that Raplie M. Cheshire be Recertified for Appointment
summary: Directed the Civil Service Commission to reissue a 1901 certificate naming Raplie M. Cheshire, who had declined the appointment by mistake.

title: Authorizing Appointment of David Lynch for Duty in the Signal Service Without Examination Under Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed David Lynch to be appointed cable engineer for the Signal Service in Manila without civil-service examination.

title: Nambe Pueblo Indian Reservation, New Mexico Territory, established for the use and occupation of the Indians of the Nambe Pueblo, subject to valid existing rights.
summary: Established the Nambe Pueblo Indian Reservation in New Mexico Territory for the use and occupation of the Nambe Pueblo Indians, subject to valid existing rights.

title: Closing of all Executive Departments for Observance of the Grand Army of the Republic Parade, October 8, 1902
summary: Closed the executive departments, the Government Printing Office and the Washington navy yard so federal workers could join or honor the Grand Army of the Republic parade of October 8, 1902.

title: Authorizing Retention of Workers on Government Printing Office Building Construction Without Regard to Civil Service Rules During Work on War College and Washington Barracks
summary: Let workers on the Government Printing Office building be kept on, without regard to civil-service rules, for work on the War College and Washington Barracks.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Apportionment Striking Section 6 of Rule VIII
summary: Struck section 6 of Civil Service Rule VIII, changing the rules on apportionment of appointments.

title: Ordering Reaffirmation and Enforcement of Regulations Governing the Soliciting of Contributions for Political Purposes by and From Government Officers or Employees
summary: Directed that the rules against soliciting political contributions from federal officers and employees be reaffirmed and enforced, after an Attorney General's opinion on circulars sent by party committees in Pennsylvania and Ohio.

title: Thanksgiving Day, 1902
summary: Named Thursday, November 27, 1902, a national day of thanksgiving.

title: Amending Consular Regulations of 1896, Paragraph 660, to Except Gold or Silver Bullion as Money or Currency
summary: Amended paragraph 660 of the 1896 Consular Regulations so gold or silver bullion is not counted as money or currency.

title: Malaga Military Reservation, Samar Island Province, P. I., established.
summary: Established the Malaga Military Reservation in Samar Island Province, Philippine Islands.

title: Fort William H. Seward Military Reservation, Haines, Alaska (est. by EO of Dec. 31, 1898), enlarged to include a clay deposit for road-making; east shore of Chilkat Inlet near Dyea reserved for military purposes.
summary: Enlarged the Fort William H. Seward Military Reservation at Haines, Alaska, to take in a clay deposit for road-making, and reserved the east shore of Chilkat Inlet near Dyea for military use.

title: Greenville Indian Industrial Training School Reservation, Calif., enlarged by addition of certain described lands.
summary: Added described lands to the Greenville Indian Industrial Training School Reservation in California.

title: Olongapo Naval Station, Zambales Province, Island of Luzon, P. I., established.
summary: Established the Olongapo Naval Station in Zambales Province on Luzon, Philippine Islands.

title: Duties of Secretary to the President Defined
summary: Defined the duties of the Secretary to the President.

title: White Mountain or San Carlos Indian Reservation, Arizona Territory, diminished and certain described lands restored to the public domain.
summary: Shrank the White Mountain or San Carlos Indian Reservation in Arizona Territory, returning described lands to the public domain.

title: Authorizing Appointment of F. L. Templeton as Clerk in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Authorized F. L. Templeton's appointment as a clerk in the Post Office Department without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles W. Newton as Physician in Western Navajo Agency Without Examination
summary: Allowed Charles W. Newton to be appointed physician at the Western Navajo Agency without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Stainslaus M. Hamilton as Clerk in Department of State Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Authorized reinstating Stainslaus M. Hamilton as a clerk in the Department of State without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Extension of Temporary Appointment of Eight Clerks in Internal Revenue Service for Sixty Days
summary: Extended the temporary appointments of eight Internal Revenue Service clerks for sixty days.

title: Establishment of the Luquillo Forest Reserve
summary: Set apart public lands in the Luquillo area of Puerto Rico as the Luquillo Forest Reserve, defining its limits by latitude and longitude and reserving it from settlement.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Require Certification of Laborers Who Perform Work of Grade of Classified Employees
summary: Amended the civil service rules to require certification of laborers who do the work of classified employees.

title: Placing the Midway Islands Under the Jurisdiction and Control of the Navy Department
summary: Put the Midway Islands under the jurisdiction and control of the Navy Department.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Prohibit Certain Transfers if Position Can be Filled by Promotion
summary: Amended the civil-service rules to bar certain transfers when a position could be filled by promotion.

title: Enlargement of the Yellowstone National Reserve
summary: Merged the Yellowstone, Teton and Absaroka forest reserves, with added lands, into a single Yellowstone Forest Reserve spanning Wyoming and Montana, superseding earlier proclamations and protecting existing rights.

title: Authorizing Appointment of F. A. Collins as Private Secretary to the Public Printer Without Examination
summary: Allowed F. A. Collins to be appointed private secretary to the Public Printer without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Oscar Wenderoth as Senior Draftsman in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Authorized reinstating Oscar Wenderoth as senior draftsman in the Treasury Department without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Partial Revocation of Withdrawal From Sioux Indian Lands
summary: Opened to disposal the former Cheyenne River Agency tract on Sioux lands along the Missouri River, since the agency and school buildings had moved, except 160 acres held by the St. Johns Mission School.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Temporary Clerks at Naval Stations in Insular Possessions
summary: Permitted temporary clerks at naval stations in the insular possessions to receive permanent appointments.

title: Removing Civil Service Rule Provision which Allowed Aliens to Qualify for Copperplate Map Engraver Position
summary: Removed the civil-service rule provision that had let aliens qualify for the position of copperplate map engraver.

title: Convening the Senate of the United States
summary: Called the U.S. Senate into extraordinary session at the Capitol at noon on March 5, 1903.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Translator in Bureau of Insular Affairs Without Examination
summary: Authorized appointing a translator in the Bureau of Insular Affairs without examination.

title: Transferring Revolutionary Archives from the State Department to the Library of Congress
summary: Moved the State Department's Revolutionary archives, including the Continental Congress records and the papers of Washington, Madison, Jefferson, Hamilton, Monroe and Franklin, to the Library of Congress for preservation and public use.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Horatio C. Pollock as Clerk at Military Headquarters in Philippine Islands Without Examination
summary: Authorized Horatio C. Pollock's appointment as a clerk at military headquarters in the Philippine Islands without examination.

title: Valdez Signal Supply Station, east shore of Valdez Bay, Alaska, established for the Signal Corps.
summary: Established the Valdez Signal Station on the east shore of Valdez Bay, Alaska, for the Signal Corps' Fort Liscum–Fort Egbert military telegraph line.

title: Authorizing Appointment of William J. Lee as Telegrapher in Department of Commerce and Labor Without Examination
summary: Allowed William J. Lee to be appointed telegrapher in the Department of Commerce and Labor without examination.

title: Pelican Island Reservation, Fla., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
summary: Set aside Pelican Island in Florida's Indian River as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, with its boundaries described.

title: Prescribing Civil Service Rules in Lieu of Rules of May 6, 1896
summary: Issued a new set of civil-service rules replacing those of May 6, 1896, barring political or religious tests and coercion and requiring examinations for the classified service.

title: Appointment of Unclassified Laborers Outside of Washington, D.C.
summary: Directed the Civil Service Commission to help departments set up competitive registration of laborers and workmen in offices outside Washington, starting in large cities.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James A. Dumont as Inspector of Hulls in Steamboat Inspection Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Authorized James A. Dumont's appointment as inspector of hulls in the Steamboat Inspection Service without regard to civil-service rules.

title: St. Cloud, Minn., Land Office (St. Cloud Land District) transferred to Cass Lake; described lands shifted among the St. Cloud, Marshall, Crookston and Duluth Land Districts.
summary: Moved the St. Cloud, Minnesota, land office to Cass Lake and shifted described lands among the St. Cloud, Marshall, Crookston and Duluth land districts.

title: Marshall, Minn., Land Office directed removed to St. Cloud effective July 1, 1903.
summary: Ordered the Marshall, Minnesota, land office moved to St. Cloud, effective July 1, 1903.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Exum L. Holland to Inspector in Customs Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Authorized Exum L. Holland's transfer to inspector in the Customs Service without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Clarifying that Civil Service Rules of March 20, 1903 do not give Permanent Appointment to Employees Serving under Rule VIII, Sections 13-16 of Rules of 1896
summary: Clarified that the civil-service rules of March 20, 1903, did not give permanent appointments to employees serving under sections 13-16 of Rule VIII of the 1896 rules.

title: Requiring Executive Departments to Furnish Information to Secretary of the Interior for Preparation of Official Register
summary: Required the executive departments to furnish the Secretary of the Interior with information for preparing the Official Register.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Albert U. Wyman as Clerk in Office of the Treasurer Without Examination
summary: Allowed Albert U. Wyman to be appointed clerk in the Office of the Treasurer without examination.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Lucas Blanco as Messenger in Customs Service Without Examination
summary: Authorized a permanent appointment for Lucas Blanco as messenger in the Customs Service without examination.

title: Skagway Military Reservation, Skagway, Alaska (466.12 acres), established.
summary: Established the Skagway Military Reservation, 466.12 acres at Skagway, Alaska.

title: Establishment of the Manti Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Manti Forest Reserve in Utah, setting out its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.

title: Establishment of the Logan Forest Reserve
summary: Established the Logan Forest Reserve in Utah, describing its limits and closing the land to settlement.

title: Torrey Barracks Military Reservation, Malabang, Island of Mindanao, P. I., established, and boundaries defined.
summary: Established the Torrey Barracks Military Reservation at Malabang on Mindanao, Philippine Islands, and defined its boundaries.

title: Certain described lands in the St. Cloud, Minn., Land District transferred to the Duluth Land District, effective June 30, 1903.
summary: Transferred described lands from the St. Cloud, Minnesota, land district to the Duluth land district, effective June 30, 1903.

title: Amending Consular Regulations of 1896, Paragraph 463, on Issuance of Circulars
summary: Amended paragraph 463 of the Consular Regulations of 1896 on the issuing of circulars.

title: Establishing the Lewis and Clark Forest Reserve in Montana
summary: Combined the Lewis and Clarke and Flathead forest reserves in Montana into one Lewis and Clarke Forest Reserve with new boundaries, adding some lands, dropping others, and setting a date for excluded lands to open.

title: Isabela de Basilan Reservation (Zamboanga), Poloc Reservation (Parang), and Fort San Pedro (Cebu), P. I., reserved for naval purposes.
summary: Reserved the Isabela de Basilan Reservation at Zamboanga, the Poloc Reservation at Parang and Fort San Pedro at Cebu, Philippine Islands, for naval purposes.

title: Reservation of Lands in Puerto Rico for Naval Purposes
summary: Reserved described public lands in Puerto Rico for naval purposes under the 1902 act letting the President keep federal lands on the island for public uses.

title: Certain described lands in Puerto Rico reserved for naval purposes.
Certain Property at Ponce, Mayaguez, and San Juan, Porto Rico, Reserved for Use of Courts, District Attorney, and Marshal
summary: Reserved property at Ponce, Mayaguez and San Juan, Puerto Rico, for the use of the federal courts, district attorney and marshal.

title: Reservation of Lands in Puerto Rico
summary: Kept described federal lands in Puerto Rico for public uses, including a public building site in San Juan, a marine hospital, custom-houses and lighthouses.

title: Right to Amend or Modify the Proclamation of June 26, 1903, Reserving Lands in Puerto Rico for Naval Purposes, Reserved; Submission of Memoranda on Use of the Lands Permitted
summary: Reserved the right to amend the June 26, 1903 proclamation setting aside Puerto Rico lands for the Navy, and allowed the Navy Secretary and the Governor of Puerto Rico to submit memoranda on how the lands would be used.

title: Eliminating Lands and Building Known as The Presidio, San Juan, Porto Rico, from Operation of Proclamation of June 26, 1903
summary: Withdrew The Presidio, the penitentiary grounds and buildings at San Juan, from the June 26, 1903, proclamation reserving Puerto Rico lands for naval use.

title: Certain described lands in Puerto Rico reserved for military purposes.
summary: Established a group of military reservations across Puerto Rico, including Aibonito, Aguadilla, Fajardo, Henry Barracks at Cayey, Mayagüez, San Juan and sites around San Juan Harbor.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Charles B. Terry as Clerk in Post Office Department Without Examination
summary: Authorized reinstating Charles B. Terry as a clerk in the Post Office Department after he had been shifted off the temporary roll and missed classification.

title: Prescribing Manner of Examination for Unskilled Labor Positions and Veterans of the Civil War
summary: Dropped the age requirement from unskilled-labor tests for Civil War soldiers and sailors, judging them instead on physical fitness, character, industry and adaptability for manual labor.

title: Nonucan (later Camp Overton) Military Reservation, Mindanao, P. I., established.
summary: Established the Nonucan Military Reservation, later Camp Overton, on Mindanao, Philippine Islands.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Ten Persons to Positions in Department of Commerce and Labor Without Examination
summary: Approved appointing ten people to positions in the Department of Commerce and Labor without civil-service examination, citing each one's special qualifications.

title: Ten specified persons appointed to the Commerce and Labor Department, without examination.
Authorizing Reinstatement of Sarah McLanahan as Sewer in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived the one-year reinstatement limit so Sarah McLanahan, widowed with three children, could return as a sewer at the Government Printing Office.

title: Regularly detailed Navy gun captains granted five dollars additional monthly pay.
summary: Granted Navy gun captains on regular detail five dollars a month in extra pay.

title: Approving the Extension of Certain Temporary Employees Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Approved Civil Service Commission extensions of temporary job employments beyond six months, covering carpenters, clerks and other workers at posts from Monterey to Fort Niagara.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Annie M. West and Sadie B. Yates to Positions in Government Printing Office
summary: Let Annie M. West and Sadie B. Yates be reinstated as sewer and telephone operator at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year reinstatement limit.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Luther M. Walter as Law Clerk in Interstate Commerce Commission Upon Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed Luther M. Walter to be appointed law clerk in the Interstate Commerce Commission after a noncompetitive examination.

title: Camp Hartshorne Military Reservation, Laguan, Samar Island, P. I., established.
summary: Established the Camp Hartshorne Military Reservation at Laguan, Samar Island, Philippine Islands.

title: Moapa River (Paiute) Indian Reservation, Nev., enlarged by certain described lands.
summary: Enlarged the Moapa River (Paiute) Indian Reservation in Nevada by adding certain described lands.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to March 2, 1904
summary: Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission six more months, past September 2, 1903, to finish judging American citizens' claims against Spain under the 1898 treaty.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Julia W. Wellborn as Clerk in the Geological Survey Without Examination
summary: Allowed Julia W. Wellborn to be permanently appointed a clerk in the Geological Survey without a civil-service examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Exceptions from Examination
summary: Amended the civil-service rules to drop the exception from examination for one clerk at each pension agency who stood in for the agent during absence or disability.

title: Revocation of Withdrawal for Day County Seat in Cheyenne and Arapaho Indian Reservation
summary: Restored to settlement a half-section in the former Cheyenne and Arapahoe lands of Oklahoma Territory once held for Day County's county seat, which had moved to the town of Grand in 1893.

title: Authorizing Employment of Allen Hazen as Engineer in Washington Filtration Plant for Two Years
summary: Let consulting engineer Allen Hazen stay on through construction and early operation of the Washington filtration plant, for no more than 24 months.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Dr. William A. White as Superintendent of the Government Hospital for the Insane Without Examination
summary: Allowed Dr. William A. White to fill the vacant superintendent's post at the Government Hospital for the Insane without a civil-service examination.

title: Authorizing Transfer of W. E. Lackland to Post-Office at Prescott, Arizona, Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived the six-month service requirement so W. E. Lackland could transfer from the Treasury Department to the post office at Prescott, Arizona.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Emma J. Rawlings as Teller in the Treasury Department
summary: Approved reinstating Emma J. Rawlings, a former expert money teller and daughter of a Civil War veteran, to the Treasury Department post her mother had held.

title: Fifteen Philippine military reservations established in one order (Camp Stotsenberg at Angeles, Camp McGrath at Batangas, and others).
summary: Set up fifteen military reservations across the Philippines in a single order, including Camp Stotsenberg at Angeles and Camp McGrath at Batangas.

title: Establishment of the Pocatello Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Pocatello Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Rules Governing the Granting and Issuing of Passports in the United States
summary: Laid out the rules for U.S. passports: only the Secretary of State issues them, only those owing allegiance qualify, and applicants must file a sworn, attested application with personal details.

title: Abandoned Camp McDowell Military Reservation, Maricopa County, Arizona Territory, set aside for the Mojave-Apache Indians living on or near it and other Indians the Interior Secretary might place there.
summary: Set aside the abandoned Camp McDowell Military Reservation in Maricopa County, Arizona Territory, for the Mojave-Apache Indians living on or near it and for other Indians the Secretary of the Interior might later place there.

title: Siassi Military Reservation, Moro Province, P. I., established as a pipe-line right of way.
summary: Established the Siassi Military Reservation in Moro Province, Philippines, as a right of way for a pipe line.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Clarence A. Cook as Special Agent in Department of Commerce and Labor Without Examination
summary: Allowed Clarence A. Cook to be appointed a special agent of the Bureau of Corporations at $2,000 a year without a civil-service examination.

title: Fort D. A. Russell Target and Maneuver Reservation, on lands of the Crow Creek Forest Reserve, Albany County, Wyo., established.
summary: Turned the former Crow Creek Forest Reserve in Albany County, Wyoming, into the Fort D. A. Russell Target and Maneuver Reservation.

title: Fort San Pedro Military Reservation, Iloilo, Island of Panay, P. I., established.
summary: Established the Fort San Pedro Military Reservation at Iloilo on the island of Panay in the Philippines.

title: Baguio (later Camp John Hay) Military Reservation, Benguet Province, Luzon, P. I., 535.63 acres, established.
summary: Created a 535.63-acre military reservation at Baguio in Benguet Province, Luzon, in the Philippines.

title: Convening Extraordinary Session of Congress
summary: Called both houses of Congress into extraordinary session on November 9, 1903, to decide whether to approve the reciprocal trade convention with Cuba signed at Havana.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Lillian B. Kellogg as Sewer in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Lillian B. Kellogg to return as a piece sewer at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Establishment of the Aquarius Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Aquarius Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Thanksgiving Day, 1903
summary: Named Thursday, November 26, 1903, a national day of thanksgiving, asking Americans to set aside their usual work and give thanks in their homes and places of worship.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mrs. Roy L. Quackenbush as Clerk in Post Office Department Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mrs. Roy L. Quackenbush, a temporary Post-Office Department clerk, to be made permanent without examination.

title: Enlargement of the Payson Forest Reserve
summary: Enlarged the Payson Forest Reserve in Utah, first established in 1901, to take in additional described lands.

title: EO of June 30, 1903 (Puerto Rico military/lighthouse lands) modified.
summary: Modified the June 30, 1903, order setting aside military and lighthouse lands in Puerto Rico.

title: Extending Benefits of Copyright Law to Citizens of Cuba
summary: Extended U.S. copyright protection to citizens of Cuba after assurances that Cuban law gives Americans copyright on the same basis as its own citizens.

title: EO of June 30, 1903 (Puerto Rico military/lighthouse lands) further modified.
summary: Further modified the June 30, 1903, order setting aside military and lighthouse lands in Puerto Rico.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Francis L. Hawes as Special Agent in Bureau of Corporations Without Examination
summary: Allowed Francis L. Hawes of New York to be appointed a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations at $1,600 a year without examination.

title: Prohibiting Use of Official Letterheads and Signatures by Consular Officers on Private Correspondence
summary: Barred consular officers from using official letterheads and signatures on private correspondence.

title: Reserving All Lands on Certain Alaska Islands, including Kiska Island, Little Kiska Island, and Adjacent Islets For Naval Purposes
summary: Reserved all land on Kiska Island, Little Kiska Island and nearby islets in Alaska for naval purposes.

title: Establishment of the Highwood Mountains Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Highwood Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Red Bank Military Reservation, N. J. (100 acres), diminished by transfer of a 400-sq-ft monument site to the Interior Department.
summary: Trimmed the Red Bank Military Reservation in New Jersey by handing a 400-square-foot monument site to the Interior Department.

title: Establishment of the Santa Barbara Forest Reserve
summary: Combined the Pine Mountain and Zaca Lake and the Santa Ynez forest reserves, plus added lands, into a single new Santa Barbara Forest Reserve in California.

title: Lighthouses in Hawaii
summary: Took over the former Republic of Hawaii's lighthouses, nearby land, buoys, beacons and records for the United States, placing them under the Light-House Board of the Department of Commerce and Labor.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mrs. Frank L. Harrigan as Machine Feeder in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. Frank L. Harrigan to return as a ruling machine feeder at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Fort Liscum Military Reservation, Port Valdez, Alaska (est. EO July 18, 1900), diminished to 659.89 acres.
summary: Shrank the Fort Liscum Military Reservation at Port Valdez, Alaska, to 659.89 acres.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Evelyn M. Ford as Clerk in the War Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Evelyn M. Ford to be reinstated as a clerk in the office of the Secretary of War despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Grant of Fort Marcy Military Reservation to the Town of Santa Fe, New Mexico
summary: Granted the abandoned Fort Marcy Military Reservation, about 17¾ acres, to the town of Santa Fe, New Mexico, which had agreed to hand it to the Board of Education to support public schools.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mrs. G. W. Shipman as Clerk in Office of the First Assistant Postmaster-General Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mrs. G. W. Shipman to be appointed a clerk in the Office of the First Assistant Postmaster-General without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Elizabeth C. Peters as Sewer in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Elizabeth C. Peters to return as a sewer at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Guantánamo Bay Military Reservation, Cuba, established.
summary: Established the Guantánamo Bay Military Reservation in Cuba.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to September 2, 1904
summary: Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission another six months, past March 2, 1904, to finish judging American citizens' claims against Spain.

title: Fort Yates Military Reservation, N. Dak. (est. Dec. 23, 1874), transferred to Interior for the Indian Service.
summary: Transferred the Fort Yates Military Reservation in North Dakota to the Interior Department for use by the Indian Service.

title: Oklahoma (City) Land District abolished; lands and Land Office business/archives transferred to the Guthrie district and office.
summary: Abolished the Oklahoma (City) land district, moving its lands, business and records to the Guthrie district and land office.

title: Fort Egbert Military Reservation, Alaska (est. EO June 13, 1899), further diminished.
summary: Further reduced the Fort Egbert Military Reservation in Alaska.

title: Pine Ridge Sioux Indian Reservation, S. Dak., diminished by restoring to the public domain the Nebraska lands added by EO of Jan. 24, 1882.
summary: Shrank the Pine Ridge Sioux Indian Reservation by returning to the public domain the Nebraska lands added to it in January 1882.

title: Authorizing Appointment of E. W. Libbey as Operator in Department of Commerce and Labor without Examination
summary: Approved E. W. Libbey's July 1903 appointment as telegraph and telephone operator in the Department of Commerce and Labor and let him stay without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Kate L. Croggan as Sewer in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Kate L. Croggan to return as a sewer at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Authority to lease certain Alaskan islands for fox propagation transferred from the Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of Commerce and Labor.
summary: Moved the authority to lease certain Alaskan islands for fox raising from the Treasury Secretary to the Secretary of Commerce and Labor.

title: Establishing the Baker City Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Baker City Forest Reserve in Oregon, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Authorizing Employment of James M. Cooper and Ralston Williams by Medical Board Investigating Typhoid Fever
summary: Let James M. Cooper and Ralston Williams work for the Army medical board studying typhoid fever in the 1898 military camps until its report was done.

title: Revoking Special Civil Service Rule of July 3, 1902, Pertaining to Persons Formerly Employed in Military Government of Cuba
summary: Revoked the July 3, 1902, special rule that let former employees of the U.S. military government of Cuba move into matching classified-service jobs.

title: Allowing Transfer of Matthew J. McCarthy from Excepted Position of Special Deputy Surveyor to Deputy Surveyor and Inspector at Customs Port of Syracuse, N.Y., Without Examination
summary: Allowed Matthew J. McCarthy to transfer without examination from the excepted post of special deputy surveyor to deputy surveyor and inspector at the customs port of Syracuse, New York.

title: Declaration of Neutrality in the War Between Japan and Russia
summary: Declared U.S. neutrality in the war between Japan and Russia, warning Americans against aiding either side and laying out rules on belligerent vessels, contraband and neutral rights at sea.

title: Parang (later Ludlow Barracks) Military Reservation, Moro/Cotabato Province, Mindanao, P. I., 1,159 acres, established.
summary: Established a 1,159-acre military reservation at Parang in Mindanao, Philippines.

title: Authorizing Certification of Marie L. Baldwin as Clerk in Office of Indian Affairs Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Marie L. Baldwin, on the Minnesota clerk register, to be certified as a $900 clerk in the Office of Indian Affairs, setting aside Rule VII.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Commissioners of National Military Parks from Examination
summary: Added all commissioners of the national military parks to the War Department positions exempt from civil-service examination.

title: Ordering federal Offices in Ohio Closed on February 19, 1904 for Funeral Services of Marcus A. Hanna
summary: Closed all federal offices in Ohio during the funeral of Senator Marcus A. Hanna on February 19, 1904, as a mark of respect.

title: EO of Jan. 25, 1904 amended to reserve permanently the irrigation-ditch and school-pasture section of the Pine Ridge Boarding School, Nebr.
summary: Amended a January 1904 order to permanently reserve the section holding the irrigation ditch and school pasture of the Pine Ridge Boarding School in Nebraska.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Francis Walker as Special Agent in Bureau of Corporations Without Examination
summary: Allowed Francis Walker of Massachusetts to be appointed a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations at $2,000 a year without examination.

title: Designating All Position Except Laborers in Civil Service of War Department in Philippines as Classified Under Civil Service Rules
summary: Brought nearly every War Department civil-service job in the Philippines under the classified civil service, except laborers and presidential appointees, and set terms for retaining current workers.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Merrit O. Chance to Superintendent in Post Office Department Without Examination
summary: Allowed Merrit O. Chance to move from clerk to the Secretary of War to superintendent of post-office supplies without a noncompetitive examination.

title: Establishing the Cave Hills Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Cave Hills Forest Reserve in South Dakota, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Establishing the Slim Buttes Forest Reserve
summary: Created the Slim Buttes Forest Reserve in South Dakota, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Granting Fort Marcy Reservation Lands to Santa Fe, New Mexico
summary: Corrected and reissued the grant of the abandoned Fort Marcy Military Reservation to the town of Santa Fe, New Mexico, for public use in support of its public schools.

title: Further Reaffirming the Observance of Proclamation of February 11, 1904 by All Officials of the Government
summary: Directed all civil, military and naval officials to observe the neutrality proclamation in the Russia–Japan war and avoid any act or speech that could irritate either combatant.

title: Manila Bay Military Reservations (est. EO Apr. 11, 1902) diminished.
summary: Reduced the Manila Bay Military Reservations in the Philippines, first set aside in April 1902.

title: Mariveles Military Reservation, Bataan Province, Luzon, P. I., redefined.
summary: Redefined the Mariveles Military Reservation in Bataan Province, Luzon, Philippines.

title: Boundary between the Boise and Lewiston, Idaho, Land Districts modified, effective May 2, 1904.
summary: Shifted the boundary between the Boise and Lewiston land districts in Idaho, effective May 2, 1904.

title: Sangley Point Military Reservation, Cañacao Bay, Luzon, P. I. (~2 acres within the naval reservation), established.
summary: Established the Sangley Point Military Reservation, about two acres inside the naval reservation on Cañacao Bay, Luzon, Philippines.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Physicians in Indian Service
summary: Widened a civil-service exception so contract physicians anywhere in the Indian service, not just at Indian schools, earning up to $720 a year could keep a private practice.

title: Compensation of members of the Isthmian Canal Commission prescribed.
summary: Set the pay for members of the Isthmian Canal Commission.

title: Restoring to the Public Domain Certain Lands Adjacent to the City of Lawton, Oklahoma Territory
summary: Returned 120 acres once reserved for the Fort Sill Indian boarding school to the public domain so the adjoining city of Lawton, Oklahoma Territory, could claim it for a park.

title: Disposal of Sioux Lands
summary: Opened to disposal the 160-acre St. John's Mission School tract near the Cheyenne River Agency in South Dakota after the missionary society gave up its use.

title: Enlargement of the Fish Lake Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Enlarged the Fish Lake Forest Reserve in Utah, established in 1899, by redrawing its boundaries to take in more land.

title: Reserving Certain Lands Within the Hailey Land District
summary: Reserved tracts in Idaho's Hailey land district for future townsites along a proposed railroad through lands to be irrigated under the Reclamation Act.

title: Reducing Area of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, Wyoming and Montana
summary: Redrew the Yellowstone Forest Reserve in Wyoming and Montana, adding some land but removing far more, for a net reduction of the reserve.

title: Establishment of the Grantsville Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Created the Grantsville Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Opening of Sioux Lands of the Rosebud Reservation, South Dakota
summary: Opened about 382,000 acres of Rosebud Reservation land in Gregory County, South Dakota, ceded by the Sioux, to settlement, while holding back tracts for a sub-issue station, day school and missions.

title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve in Colorado and set a date for opening lands left outside to settlement.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Katherine C. Masterson in Government Printing Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Katherine C. Masterson to be reinstated at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Modification of the Boundaries of the White River Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Further redrew the boundaries of the White River Forest Reserve in Colorado and set a date for opening lands left outside to settlement.

title: Establishment of the Salt Lake Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Created the Salt Lake Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.

title: Authorizing Appointment of I. B. Conklin as Clerk in Washington Navy Yard Without Examination
summary: Allowed I. B. Conklin to be hired as a clerk at $3.28 a day in the paymaster's office of the Washington Navy Yard without examination.

title: Partial Opening of Lands of the Sisseton, Wahpeton and Cut-Head Bands of the Sioux Indian Tribe
summary: Opened about 88,000 acres of the Devils Lake Reservation in North Dakota, including the old Fort Totten Military Reserve, ceded by Sisseton, Wahpeton and Cut-Head Sioux, to homestead and townsite entry.

title: Certain N. Dak. lands transferred from the Grand Forks to the Devils Lake Land District, effective Aug. 1, 1904.
summary: Moved certain North Dakota lands from the Grand Forks land district to the Devils Lake land district, effective August 1, 1904.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Promotion to Former Positions
summary: Changed the civil-service rules so a person reinstated at a lower grade can be promoted back to the former grade without examination.

title: Diminution of Bitter Root Forest Reserve, Idaho and Montana
summary: Cut described lands in Idaho out of the Bitter Root Forest Reserve and restored them to the public domain, with a set date for opening them to settlement.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Samuel D. Amen as Internal Revenue Agent Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Made an exception to the civil-service rules so Samuel D. Amen could be appointed an internal-revenue agent.

title: Pasay Military Reservation (Rizal Province, ~96.6 acres) and Zamboanga/Pettit Barracks (Mindanao, ~131 acres), P. I., established.
summary: Established two Philippine military reservations: about 96.6 acres at Pasay in Rizal Province and about 131 acres at Zamboanga (Pettit Barracks) on Mindanao.

title: Fort Niobrara Military Reservation, Cherry County, Nebr. (est. EO Dec. 10, 1879), enlarged by 25,900 acres to ~60,000.
summary: Enlarged the Fort Niobrara Military Reservation in Cherry County, Nebraska, by 25,900 acres, to about 60,000 acres.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Dr. William L. Ralph as Curator in National Museum Without Examination
summary: Allowed Dr. William L. Ralph to be appointed curator of birds' eggs at the National Museum, at $100 a month, without examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Clarence Reeder as Secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey Without Examination
summary: Allowed Clarence Reeder to be appointed private secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey without examination.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Edna K. Hoyt as Clerk in Department of State Without Examination
summary: Let Edna K. Hoyt, a temporary State Department clerk, be made permanent at $1,200 a year without examination, at Secretary Hay's request.

title: ~11.7 acres at Fort Santiago, Manila, P. I., reserved for an ordnance depot.
summary: Reserved about 11.7 acres at Fort Santiago in Manila, Philippines, for an ordnance depot.

title: EO of Mar. 10, 1903 amended; Valdez Signal Station, Alaska, diminished to 22,946 sq. ft.; adjoining lands reserved for War/Justice.
summary: Shrank the Valdez Signal Station in Alaska to 22,946 square feet, amending a March 10, 1903, order, and reserved the adjoining lands for the War and Justice Departments.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to March 2, 1905
summary: Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission until March 2, 1905, to finish its work.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James E. S. Kinsella as Minor Under Instruction in Navy Yard Without Regard to Navy Yard Order No. 13
summary: Allowed James E. S. Kinsella to be appointed a minor under instruction in the ordnance department of the Washington, D.C., navy yard without meeting Navy Yard Order No. 13.

title: Authorizing Promotion of Ludwick C. Young to Clerk in Census Office Without Examination
summary: Let Ludwick C. Young, a laborer in the Census Office, be promoted to clerk without examination, in view of his earlier service as a clerk there.

title: Whipple Barracks Target Range Military Reservation, Yavapai County, Arizona Territory, 1,680 acres, established.
summary: Created the Whipple Barracks Target Range Military Reservation, 1,680 acres in Yavapai County, Arizona Territory.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Dr. William Conyngton as Physician at Grand River Indian School After Special Examination'
summary: Permitted Dr. William Conyngton to be permanently appointed physician at the Grand River Indian School in North Dakota after a special examination, needed because illness at the school was rising and every eligible candidate had declined.

title: EO of Mar. 25, 1904 (Sangley Point Military Reservation) amended.
summary: Amended the March 25, 1904, order concerning the Sangley Point Military Reservation.

title: Breton Island Reservation, St. Bernard and Plaquemines Parishes, La., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
summary: Established the Breton Island reservation for wildlife in St. Bernard and Plaquemines Parishes, Louisiana.

title: Ordering Mourning Formalities for Death of Henry Clay Payne, Postmaster General
summary: Announced the death of Postmaster General Henry Clay Payne, closed the departments in Washington on the morning of his funeral, and ordered flags on public buildings nationwide flown at half-mast until he was buried.

title: Granting Land to Woodward, Oklahoma
summary: Returned a four-acre lot in Woodward, Oklahoma Territory, once held as a county courthouse site, to the public domain so it could go to the Town of Woodward for a public park.

title: Thanksgiving Day, 1904
summary: Set apart Thursday, November 24, 1904, as a national day of thanksgiving for a year of peace, abundant harvests and prosperity.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Luther Conant, Jr., as Special Examiner in Bureau of Corporations Without Examination
summary: Allowed Luther Conant, Jr., to be appointed a special examiner in the Bureau of Corporations, at $2,500 a year, without a civil-service examination.

title: Philippine military reservations: Jolo (~339.7 acres), Daraga/Regan Barracks (~318.8 acres), and Augur Barracks incl. Asturias (~535.7 acres).
summary: Reserved military land in the Philippines at Jolo (about 339.7 acres), Daraga's Regan Barracks (about 318.8 acres) and Augur Barracks, including Asturias (about 535.7 acres).

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Positions Excepted from Examination for Isthmian Canal Commission Personnel
summary: Exempted top Isthmian Canal Commission posts from civil-service examination, among them its secretary, treasurer, auditor, chief engineer, the Canal Zone governor's executive secretary, and sanitary, hospital and quarantine officers.

title: Applying Civil Service Rules to Employees of Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Brought the Isthmian Canal Commission under the civil-service act and rules, so that most officers and employees, apart from laborers, Senate-confirmed officials and detailed Army engineers, must pass an examination before being hired or promoted.

title: Regulations Governing the Appointment of Unclassified Laborers in the Departments at Washington, D.C.
summary: Set rules for hiring unskilled laborers in the departments at Washington, with a labor employment board under the Civil Service Commission rating applicants on physical fitness for manual work as judged by federal physicians.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Clare A. Cooper as Matron in Immigration Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed Clare A. Cooper to be permanently appointed matron in the Immigration Service without examination.

title: Restoring Customs Service Cashiers and Deputies to the Competitive Service
summary: Returned several Customs Service posts, including deputy or assistant collector, deputy naval officer, deputy surveyor and cashier, to the competitive service, so they now require examination.

title: Establishment of the Warner Mountains Forest Reserve, California
summary: Created the Warner Mountains Forest Reserve in California, closing the timbered public lands within its boundaries to entry and settlement.

title: Establishment of the Modoc Forest Reserve, California
summary: Established the Modoc Forest Reserve in northern California along the state line, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.

title: Designating Substitute Watchmen in Government Printing Office as Classified Under Civil Service Rules
summary: Classified substitute watchmen at the Government Printing Office under the civil-service rules, including the forty men already serving on the Public Printer's list.

title: Prohibiting Appointment in Executive Departments for Any Service of Character Performed by Classified Employees Except Under Civil Service Rules
summary: Barred executive departments from hiring anyone to do the work of classified employees except under the civil-service rules, and sent doubtful cases to the Civil Service Commission and, failing agreement, to the Attorney General.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James Rankin Young as Superintendent of Dead Letter Office Without Examination
summary: Allowed James Rankin Young of Pennsylvania to be appointed Superintendent of the Dead Letter Office without examination.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Marcus Braun as Inspector in Immigration Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed Marcus Braun to be permanently appointed an immigrant inspector in the Immigration Service without examination.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Joseph Watkinson as Assistant Inspector in Steamboat Inspection Service Without Examination
summary: Permitted Capt. Joseph Watkinson to be permanently appointed assistant inspector of hulls in the Steamboat Inspection Service without examination.

title: Diminution of the South Platte Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Reduced the South Platte Forest Reserve in Colorado, releasing some lands back to the public domain for later settlement while keeping the rest reserved.

title: EO of Sept. 1, 1903 modified; Camp Eldridge Military Reservation, Los Baños, Luzon (68.35 acres), enlarged.
summary: Enlarged the Camp Eldridge Military Reservation at Los Baños, Luzon, listed at 68.35 acres, modifying an order of September 1, 1903.
