title: Waiving Civil Service Requirements of United States Citizenship for Positions on Isthmus of Panama
summary: Allowed the U.S. citizenship requirement to be waived for applicants for jobs on the Isthmus of Panama, under Civil Service Commission regulations.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Mrs. William H. Tabberah as Keeper of the Cumberland Head Light Station, New York, Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mrs. William H. Tabberah to be permanently appointed keeper of the Cumberland Head Light Station in New York without examination.

title: Regulations to Govern the Employment of Unskilled Laborers in the Federal Offices Outside of Washington, D. C.
summary: Set rules for hiring unskilled laborers in federal offices outside Washington, starting in New York, Boston, Philadelphia and St. Louis, with local civil-service boards registering applicants aged 20 to 60.

title: Classifying Employees of General Land Office of the Interior Department Involved in Protection of Forestry Reserves
summary: Placed the General Land Office employees who protect and administer the forest reserves, in the field and in Washington, under the civil-service rules, so new hires and promotions require examination.

title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Big Horn Forest Reserve, Wyoming
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the Big Horn Forest Reserve in Wyoming, setting a date for excluded lands to open to settlement.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except from Examination a Consulting Architect in the War Department for Work on the United States Military Academy
summary: Exempted from examination a consulting architect hired by the War Department to rebuild the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, New York.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment for Thirteen Clerks in the Bureau of the Census
summary: Allowed thirteen temporary clerks compiling the Philippine census in the Bureau of the Census to be permanently appointed, since the Civil Service Commission could not certify qualified eligibles.

title: Forbidding Notaries Public in Government Service to Charge Fees for Notarial Acts
summary: Barred federal employees who are also notaries public from charging fees for notarial acts done for government business, for fellow employees acting officially, or during their government work hours. Breaking the rule meant immediate dismissal.

title: Notaries public in government employ forbidden to accept compensation for notarial acts of interest to the government.
Amending Civil Service Rules to Add Further Excepted Positions on Isthmus of Panama
summary: Added more Canal Zone posts to the list exempt from civil-service examination, including judges, court officers, mayors, police and locally hired skilled tradesmen earning $4 a day or less.

title: Classification of Certain Laborers Employed in the City of Washington, District of Columbia
summary: Classified the Washington department laborers who had been doing clerical-grade work since 1902, allowing them to be promoted to clerk or transferred under the civil-service rules.

title: Joseph L. Bristow appointed Special Commissioner to investigate trans-Isthmus trade and freight rates and Panama Railroad management.
summary: Named Joseph L. Bristow special commissioner to look into trade and freight rates across the Isthmus of Panama and the management of the Panama Railroad.

title: Camp Marahui (later Camp Keithley) Military Reservation, Moro Province, Mindanao, P. I., established.
summary: Established Camp Marahui Military Reservation, later called Camp Keithley, in Moro Province on Mindanao in the Philippines.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Exceptions from Examination for Customs Service Positions in Alaska
summary: Removed Alaska's Customs Service from the blanket civil-service exemption for hard-to-fill Alaska posts, while exempting seasonal Alaska customs workers hired only for the navigation season.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to September 2, 1905
summary: Extended the deadline for the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to finish its work to September 2, 1905.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Stephen W. Fuller to Messenger in Department of Commerce and Labor Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Stephen W. Fuller, a messenger boy at the Library of Congress, to transfer to messenger in the Bureau of Manufactures, Department of Commerce and Labor.

title: Duties, records and files of the Commissioner of Railroads transferred from Interior to Commerce and Labor.
summary: Moved the duties, records and files of the Commissioner of Railroads from the Interior Department to the Department of Commerce and Labor.

title: Waiving Citizenship Requirements for Applicants for Examination for Officers of Ships of the Coast and Geodetic Survey on Duty in the Philippines
summary: Allowed the U.S. citizenship requirement to be waived for applicants seeking officer posts on Coast and Geodetic Survey ships serving in the Philippine Islands.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of George F. Otis as Clerk in Quartermaster's Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed George F. Otis to be reinstated as a clerk in the Quartermaster's Department despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.

title: Convening a Special Session of the United States Senate
summary: Called the U.S. Senate into special session at the Capitol at noon on March 4, 1905, to receive communications from the President.

title: Ordering Formation of a Commission to Investigate the Naturalization of Aliens Under Existing Laws and to Report its Findings No Later than November 15, 1905
summary: Ordered a commission to investigate the naturalization of aliens under existing laws and report by November 15, 1905.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of John Nolan as Carrier in Postal Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed John Nolan to be reinstated as a Postal Service carrier without regard to civil-service time limits.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Certain Interior Department Positions Subject to Examination
summary: Ended the examination exemption for Interior Department special agents protecting public lands and for inspectors of surveyors-general and district land offices.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Five Special Agents in Interior Department from Examination
summary: Exempted from examination five General Land Office special agents assigned to investigate fraudulent land entries and other criminal matters.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Physicians in Indian Service from Examination
summary: Exempted from examination Indian Service physicians paid no more than $720 a year who may also keep a private practice, with each hire subject to Commission approval.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Allow Appointment of Retired Army Officers as Superintendents at Indian Schools Without Examination
summary: Allowed retired Army officers to be appointed Indian school superintendents without competitive examination, at the request of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs and with the Interior Secretary's approval.

title: Creating Stump Lake Reservation, North Dakota, as Preserve and Breeding Ground for Birds
summary: Set aside four islands in Stump Lake, North Dakota, totaling 27.39 acres, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds under the Department of Agriculture, to be known as the Stump Lake Reservation.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Donald G. Mitchell as Supervisor in Interior Department Without Examination
summary: Let Donald G. Mitchell, Jr., who had supervised construction of the Government Hospital for the Insane's new buildings, stay on as supervisor of buildings and grounds without examination.

title: Enlarging Lands Set Apart and Reserved for Navajo Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Enlarged the lands set apart for the Navajo Indian Reservation in Utah.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Catharine M. Gallagher to Classified Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived civil-service rules so Mrs. Catharine M. Gallagher, who left an Interior Department clerkship in 1901, could be reinstated in a Washington department at no higher grade.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Prohibit Salary Increase of Classified Laborers Without Examination
summary: Barred laborers classified as clerks from further pay raises unless they pass the examination for promotion to the clerical grade.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Dr. Cyrus Adler as Assistant Secretary in Smithsonian Institution Without Examination
summary: Allowed Dr. Cyrus Adler to be appointed assistant secretary in charge of the library and exchanges at the Smithsonian Institution, at $2,700 a year, without examination.

title: Creating Consultative Board of Architects for Public Buildings in District of Columbia
summary: Created an unpaid consultative board of architects, chaired by Bernard R. Green, that must review the site and exterior design of every new public building in the District of Columbia before approval.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Sydnie Kennedy as Chief of Division in Isthmian Canal Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed Sydnie Kennedy to be appointed chief of division, clerk and stenographer in the Isthmian Canal Service, at $1,800 a year, without examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of W. G. Tucker as Clerk in Isthmian Canal Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed W. G. Tucker to be appointed a clerk with the Isthmian Canal Commission, at $1,500 a year, without examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mrs. M. G. Lauxmann as Writer in Coast and Geodetic Survey Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mrs. M. G. Lauxmann to be permanently appointed a writer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey without examination.

title: Compensation of Consultative Board of Architects Prescribed
summary: Set the pay of the Consultative Board of Architects.

title: Establishing the Pinal Mountains Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Created the Pinal Mountains Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.

title: Land Office at Oregon City Transferred to Portland
summary: Moved the land office at Oregon City to Portland.

title: Oregon City, Oreg., Land Office abolished (eff. June 30, 1905); business/records to the Portland office.
Approved War Sec'y recommendation that certain Minnesota lands be reserved for flowage purposes
summary: Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve certain Minnesota lands for flowage purposes.

title: Establishing the Plumas Forest Reserve, California
summary: Established the Plumas Forest Reserve in California, setting its partly timbered public lands apart from entry and settlement.

title: Revoked Executive Order 310
summary: Revoked Executive Order 310, which had set the compensation of the consultative board of architects.

title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Madison Forest Reserve
summary: Changed the boundaries of the Madison Forest Reserve in Montana, releasing some lands and opening them to settlement.

title: Authorizing Appointment of George W. Pitts as Messenger in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed George W. Pitts, a skilled laborer at Commerce and Labor, to be appointed messenger in the Post Office Department without the usual six months of prior service.

title: Celebration of the 300th Anniversary of the Founding of Jamestown, Virginia
summary: Proclaimed an international naval, marine and military celebration on Hampton Roads, Virginia, from May 13 to November 1, 1907, marking 300 years since the Jamestown settlement, and invited foreign nations to send ships and troops.

title: Certain Lands in Lakeview Land District, Oregon, Transferred to Burns Land District
summary: Shifted certain lands from the Lakeview Land District in Oregon to the Burns Land District.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Post Office Department Cashiers and Finance Clerks Subject to Examination
summary: Amended the civil service rules so Post Office Department cashiers and finance clerks hired without examination gain competitive status only on the Postmaster-General's recommendation.

title: Classifying Certain Laborers Previously Assigned to Classified Work and Forbidding Further Such Assignments
summary: Classified laborers assigned to clerical-grade work since the January 1905 order and forbade any further such assignments; laborers needed for that work must now come from civil-service registers.

title: Designating Five Substitute Watchmen in Government Printing Office as Classified under Civil Service Rules
summary: Extended the November 1904 order classifying substitute watchmen at the Government Printing Office to five more men hired after the original list.

title: Civil Service Rules Amended to Except Certain Interior Department Positions from Examination
summary: Exempted from examination the Reclamation Service's consulting engineers and a confidential clerk and record clerk for the superintendent of the Government Hospital for the Insane.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of S. F. Scott, Jr., in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed S. F. Scott, Jr., to be reinstated in the Post-Office Service despite the time limit on reinstatement.

title: Revoked Unnumbered Order of February 9, 1905, which Transferred Office of the Commissioner of Railroads to Dept of Commerce and Labor
summary: Revoked an unnumbered order of February 9, 1905, that had moved the Office of the Commissioner of Railroads to the Department of Commerce and Labor.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Certain Bureau of Immigration Positions Subject to Examination
summary: Required civil-service examination for Bureau of Immigration employees working in countries bordering the United States, narrowing an exemption for federal jobs abroad.

title: Amending Executive Order of December 31, 1904, Relating to Restrictions on Notarial Fees, to Exclude Oaths of Disinterestedness
summary: Amended the December 1904 notary-fee ban so it no longer covers oaths of disinterestedness and other oaths required by law, as long as the work is done outside office hours.

title: Reorganization of the Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Reorganized the Isthmian Canal Commission, calling its performance unsatisfactory. Set quarterly sessions on the Isthmus, a four-member quorum and an Executive Committee, and charged the Commission, under the Secretary of War, with planning and building the canal and running the Panama Railroad.

title: Establishment of the Trinity Forest Reserve, California
summary: Created the Trinity Forest Reserve in California, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Certain Firemen of War Department from Examination
summary: Excepted all firemen on War Department torpedo planters from civil service examination.

title: Amending Executive Order of August 13, 1902, to Authorize Navy Department to Discharge Men of Messmen Branch who Enlist for Summer Practice Cruises
summary: Modified an order of August 13, 1902, so the Navy Department could discharge, on request, messmen who enlist only for the Naval Academy midshipmen's summer practice cruise.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Edward H. Hareford to Forest Assistant in Department of Agriculture Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived the three-year Philippine service requirement so Edward H. Hareford could transfer to forest assistant in the Department of Agriculture.

title: Abolishing of Ironton Land District, Mo.; Transferred to Springfield Land District
summary: Abolished the Ironton Land District in Missouri and folded it into the Springfield Land District.

title: Approving War Secretary Recommendation to Reserve Certain Lands Around Subic Bay, Luzon, Philippine Islands for Military Purposes
summary: Reserved public lands on the east side of the entrance to Subig Bay, in Bataan Province on Luzon, for military purposes, subject to private rights, approving a Secretary of War recommendation.

title: Abolishing of Marysville Land District and Transferring to Sacramento Land District
summary: Abolished the Marysville Land District and transferred it to the Sacramento Land District.

title: Abolishing of Boonville Land District and Transferring to Springfield Land District
summary: Abolished the Boonville Land District and transferred it to the Springfield Land District.

title: Establishment of Uintah Land District
summary: Created the Uintah Land District.

title: Ironton, Mo., Land Office abolished (eff. June 30, 1905); to the Springfield office.
Vernal, Utah, designated the Land Office for the Uintah Land District (act of Mar. 3, 1905, 33 Stat. L. 1014).
Establishment of the Klamath Forest Reserve, California
summary: Established the Klamath Forest Reserve in northern California, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.

title: Fort Sherman Military Reservation at Coeur d'Alene, Idaho
summary: Withdrew part of the abandoned Fort Sherman Military Reservation from sale and granted it to the town of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, for a public cemetery, as the townspeople had petitioned.

title: Establishment of the Wallowa Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Created the Wallowa Forest Reserve in northeastern Oregon, closing its partly timbered public lands to entry and settlement.

title: Enlargement of the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Added lands to the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, which had been established in 1893.

title: Abolishing of Akron Land District, Colo., Transferred to Sterling Land District
summary: Abolished the Akron Land District in Colorado and moved it into the Sterling Land District.

title: Akron, Colo., Land Office abolished (eff. June 30, 1905); to the Sterling office.
Establishment of the Wenaha Forest Reserve, Oregon and Washington
summary: Created the Wenaha Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands straddling Oregon and Washington, reserving the area from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishment of the Leadville Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Set apart the Leadville Forest Reserve in Colorado as a public reservation, covering public lands described as partly timbered and excepting lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishment of the Sevier Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Established the Sevier Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Utah and closed it to settlement, apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishment of the Chesnimnus Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Reserved partly timbered public lands in northeastern Oregon as the Chesnimnus Forest Reserve, withdrawing them from settlement except for existing lawful claims.

title: Establishment of the Elkhorn Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Created the Elkhorn Forest Reserve in Montana, setting aside partly timbered public lands as a public reservation closed to settlement, apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishment of the Gunnison Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Established the Gunnison Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Colorado, reserving them from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishment of the Pikes Peak Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Combined the Pikes Peak Timber Land Reserve, the Plum Creek Timber Land Reserve and the South Platte Forest Reserve, plus added lands, into a single Pikes Peak Forest Reserve in Colorado, superseding the earlier proclamations.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Certain Law Officers in Bureau of Insular Affairs from Examination
summary: Amended Schedule A of the civil service rules so that one law officer in the War Department's Bureau of Insular Affairs could be hired without examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Carriage Driver for Treasury Secretary Without Examination
summary: Allowed a laborer to be hired, without examination, to drive the Treasury Secretary's carriage.

title: Placing Administration of Navigation Aids Under Department of Commerce and Labor
summary: Directed the Department of Commerce and Labor to take charge of lighting and buoying the waters around Guam, and to have the Light-House Establishment prepare cost estimates for Congress.

title: Restoring to the Public Domain Certain Lands in the State of California
summary: Restored to the public domain two sections of land in southern California once reserved for the Capitan Grande band of Mission Indians but left out of the band's later selection and patent.

title: Reciprocity with Panama
summary: Suspended foreign discriminating tonnage duties and imposts on Panamanian vessels and their cargoes, after Panama showed it levied no such duties on American ships, for as long as that reciprocal treatment continues.

title: Authorizing Appointment of John Ball Osborne as Chief of Bureau of Trade Relations in State Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed John Ball Osborne to be appointed chief of the State Department's Bureau of Trade Relations without regard to civil service rules.

title: Cancellation of Executive Order 302-A of March 10, 1905, and Reserving Additional Lands in Lieu Of
summary: Canceled Executive Order 302-A of March 10, 1905, and reserved additional lands in its place.

title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve
summary: Enlarged the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve by adding partly timbered lands in Colorado, redrawing the boundaries of a reserve first created in Wyoming.

title: Executive Order 310-C Amended Eliminate Lands Comprising Homestead Entry of Louis Zeph
summary: Amended Executive Order 310-C, the Minnesota flowage reservation, to leave out the lands in Louis Zeph's homestead entry.

title: Approving War Secretary Recommendation to Reserve Seven Tracts of Land in Philippine Islands for Military Purposes
summary: Reserved government properties in Manila for military use, including the Cuartel Meisic barracks, approving a Secretary of War recommendation.

title: Approving War Secretary Recommendation to Reserve Nine Additional Tracts of Land in Jolo, Philippine Islands for Military Purposes
summary: Added tracts of land at Jolo, Philippine Islands, to the existing military reservation there, subject to private rights, approving a Secretary of War recommendation.

title: Approving War Secretary Recommendation of May 15, 1905, to Amend Executive Order of June 30, 1904, Changing Borders of Military Reservation at Zamboanga, Mindanao, Philippine Islands
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the military reservation at Zamboanga, Mindanao, amending an earlier 1904 order and reserving the public lands within the new lines, subject to private rights.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Chauncey O. Howard in Bureau of Pensions from Excepted to Non-Excepted Position Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Chauncey O. Howard to move from an excepted special examiner post in the Bureau of Pensions to a similar post that is not excepted.

title: Ordering A Stipulation Be Placed In All Government Contracts Forbidding the Use of Convict Labor
summary: Required federal contracts for work in the states and adjoining territories to forbid the use of convicts sentenced to hard labor by state, territorial or municipal courts, unless law provided otherwise.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Certain Positions in the Washington, D. C. Filtration Plant Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let a superintendent, chief chemist and first assistant chemist at the Washington filtration plant be hired outside civil service rules, since the plant was expected to pass to the District of Columbia's municipal service within a year.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Eleanor Relyea Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. Eleanor Relyea to be reinstated in the departmental service without reference to civil service rules.

title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Bitter Root Forest Reserve, Idaho and Montana
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the Bitter Root Forest Reserve in Idaho and Montana, releasing some lands, including lands in Idaho, and adding other partly timbered lands.

title: Enlargement of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho
summary: Added partly timbered public lands in Idaho to the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, which had covered lands in Wyoming and Montana.

title: Authorizing Appointment of William J. Humphreys as Professor of Meteorological Physics in Weather Bureau Without Examination
summary: Allowed William J. Humphreys to be appointed professor of meteorological physics in the Weather Bureau without examination.

title: Establishment of the Henrys Lake Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Set aside the Henrys Lake Forest Reserve in Idaho on partly timbered public lands, closing it to settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Boundaries of Uintah Land District, Utah, Modified; in Form of Proclamation
summary: Changed the boundaries of the Uintah Land District in Utah, issued in the form of a proclamation.

title: Approving Acting War Secretary Recommendation of May 24, 1905 to Reserve 13 Tracts of Described Lands in Alaska for Use by the Signal Corps. United States Army
summary: Reserved lands in Alaska for the Army Signal Corps' military telegraph lines: a 100-foot right of way along more than 1,400 miles of line, plus sites for telegraph offices, storehouses, stables and wood reserves such as Central, Chestochena and Copper Center.

title: Certain lands near Central, Alaska, reserved for military purposes.
Certain lands at Summit, Alaska, reserved for military purposes.
Establishment of the Weiser Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Created the Weiser Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishment of the Sawtooth Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Established the Sawtooth Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Idaho and withdrew it from settlement, apart from existing lawful claims.

title: Redesignating the Wichita Forest Reserve, Oklahoma, as a Game Preserve
summary: Designated the entire Wichita Forest Reserve in Oklahoma Territory as a game preserve and breeding place for game animals and birds, making hunting or trapping there unlawful except under Agriculture Department regulations.

title: Establishing the Lassen Peak Forest Reserve, California
summary: Reserved partly timbered public lands in northern California as the Lassen Peak Forest Reserve, closed to settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishing the Maury Mountain Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Created the Maury Mountain Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon, withdrawing the area from settlement apart from existing lawful claims.

title: Prescribing Compensation for Enlisted Men of the Navy Detailed as Ship's Tailors
summary: Set extra monthly pay for Navy enlisted men detailed as ship's tailors ($10 to $20, depending on the ship's crew size) and as tailor's helpers ($10), with caps on their total pay.

title: Wichita Forest Reserve, Oklahoma, redesignated as a game preserve.
Establishing the Payette Forest Reserve, Idaho
countersigned_by: Francis B Loomis Acting Secretary of States
summary: Set aside the Payette Forest Reserve in Idaho on partly timbered public lands, reserved from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishing the San Juan Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Established the San Juan Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in southwestern Colorado, excepting lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Albert C. Muhse as Special Agent in Bureau of Corporations Without Examination
summary: Allowed Albert C. Muhse to be appointed a special agent of the Bureau of Corporations, at $2,000 a year, without a civil-service examination.

title: Modifying the Boundaries of the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Redrew the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve in Colorado, releasing some lands back to the public domain and adding other partly timbered lands.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Five Employees in Isthmian Canal Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived civil service rules for five Isthmian Canal Service appointments in New Orleans and Washington, D.C., two of them transfers from the Isthmus.

title: Establishing the Park Range Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Created the Park Range Forest Reserve in Colorado, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Enlarging the San Isabel Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Enlarged the San Isabel Forest Reserve in Colorado, first proclaimed in 1902, to take in additional partly timbered public lands.

title: Modifying the Boundaries of the Washington Forest Reserve, Washington
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the Washington Forest Reserve, releasing some lands and adding other partly timbered lands in the state of Washington.

title: Establishing the Wet Mountains Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Set apart the Wet Mountains Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Colorado, closed to settlement except for existing lawful claims.

title: Establishing the Cassia Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Established the Cassia Forest Reserve in southern Idaho, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Approval of War Secretary Recommendation to Reserve Grass Island, Gray's Harbor, Washington, for Military Purposes
summary: Reserved all of Grass Island in Grays Harbor, Washington, for the harbor's defense.

title: Amendment of Executive Order of March 26, 1901, Establishing Limits of Punishment for Enlisted Men of the Army
summary: Amended the 1901 order setting maximum punishments for Army enlisted men, laying out new confinement limits for desertion based on surrender or capture, time served, prior convictions and conspiracy.

title: Grass Island Military Reservation, Wash., established.
Establishing the Cochetopa Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Created the Cochetopah Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Colorado, reserving them from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Establishing the Montezuma Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Reserved partly timbered public lands in southwestern Colorado as the Montezuma Forest Reserve, closed to settlement apart from existing lawful claims.

title: Authorizing Appointment of C. H. Chapman as Copyist in General Land Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed C. H. Chapman, a Civil War veteran, to be appointed a copyist in the General Land Office without regard to civil service rules, in view of his earlier service in the Census Office.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Allow Promotions to Superintendent in Indian Service Without Examination
summary: Amended civil service Rule XI so classified Indian Service employees could be promoted without examination to superintendent of an Indian school, on the Commissioner of Indian Affairs' statement of their qualifications.

title: Waiving Civil Service Rules and Navy Yard Regulations for Laborers at Naval Hospitals
summary: Freed the hiring of skilled and unskilled laborers at naval hospitals from civil service rules and navy-yard regulations, citing hours, varied duties and pay arrangements that made those rules impracticable.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Certain Construction Workers from Examination
summary: Amended Schedule A of the civil service rules to except mechanics, skilled tradesmen and laborers on field construction or repair work who, in the Commission's view, could not be appointed from registers of eligibles.

title: Establishing the Uncompahgre Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Established the Uncompahgre Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in western Colorado, withdrawn from settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mary T. Waggaman as Clerk in Bureau of Labor Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mary T. Waggaman to be appointed a clerk in the Bureau of Labor without regard to civil service rules.

title: Designating Board of Consulting Engineers to Consider Plans for Canal Across Isthmus of Panama
summary: Named an international Board of Consulting Engineers, with General George W. Davis as chairman, to meet in Washington on September 1, 1905, and weigh plans for a canal across the Isthmus of Panama.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of James W. Plake as Copyist in Office of Indian Affairs Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed James W. Plake, an Indian, to be permanently appointed a copyist in the Office of Indian Affairs.

title: Extending Foreign Copyright Protection to Norway
summary: Extended U.S. copyright benefits to subjects of Norway, after official assurances that Norwegian law gave Americans copyright on substantially the same basis as its own citizens.

title: Announcing the Death of John Hay
summary: Announced the death of Secretary of State John Hay and ordered flags at half-mast for ten days at U.S. embassies, legations, forts, naval stations and vessels, with executive departments in Washington closed on the day of his funeral.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles W. Bell as Finance Clerk in Post-Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Approved Charles W. Bell's appointment as finance clerk at the Lowell, Massachusetts, post office, since it was authorized before the job became competitive.

title: Placing Administration of Navigation Aids for Tutuila and Other Samoan Islands Under Control of the Department of Commerce and Labor
summary: Put the Department of Commerce and Labor in charge of lights and other navigation aids for Tutuila and the other Samoan Islands east of longitude 171° west.

title: Approving Acting War Secretary Recommendation of June 30, 1905 to Reserve Lands in Seward Alaska for Military Telegraph Purposes
summary: Reserved waterfront public land at Seward, Alaska, for the Army Signal Corps' military telegraph lines, subject to private rights.

title: Forbidding the Employment of Outside Influence for All Appointments, Transfers, Promotions Etc. of Officers of the Army and Navy
summary: Declared that Army and Navy appointments, transfers and assignments would rest on official department records, not outside influence. Officers who sought outside backing would be barred from the advancement they sought; eyewitness accounts of unrecorded bravery could still be submitted.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Abram B. Frisbie as Watchman in Interior Department Without Examination
summary: Allowed Abram B. Frisbie to be permanently appointed a watchman in the Interior Department, at the Secretary's discretion, without a civil-service examination.

title: Amending Regulations Governing the Employment of Unskilled Laborers in Federal Offices Outside Washington, D.C.
summary: Amended the regulations for hiring unskilled laborers in federal offices outside Washington, D.C.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Frank B. McCown as Clerk in Quartermaster's Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Frank B. McCown to be reinstated as a clerk in the Quartermaster's Department at large, at the Secretary of War's request.

title: Authorizing Employment of Allen Hazen as Engineer in Washington Filtration Plant for Seven Additional Months
summary: Extended Allen Hazen's temporary job as consulting engineer on the Washington filtration plant, at $275 a month, for up to seven months from August 31, 1905.

title: Establishment of the Diamond Mountain Forest Reserve, California
summary: Created the Diamond Mountain Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in California, reserving it from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Adding Lands to the Uintah Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Moved certain lands out of the Uintah Indian Reservation and into the Uintah Forest Reserve in Utah, redrawing the forest reserve's boundaries.

title: Opening to Entry Lands on Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Opened the unallotted lands of the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah to settlement and entry under the homestead and townsite laws beginning August 28, 1905, setting out how applicants would register and apply.

title: Approving Acting War Secretary Recommendation to Remove 28 Acres from Fort Bayard Military Reservation, New Mexico, Erroneously Included in Private Patent
summary: Took about 28 acres out of the Fort Bayard military reservation in New Mexico and placed them under the Secretary of the Interior for disposal.

title: Extending Time and Compensation for Joseph L. Bristow, Special Panama Railroad Commissioner, to Complete Report
summary: Gave Special Panama Railroad Commissioner Joseph L. Bristow until August 15, 1905, to finish his report, with expenses, $15 a day, and an extra $2,500, paid by the Isthmian Canal Commission.

title: Modifying Boundaries of Fort Gibbon Military Reservation, Alaska
summary: Redrew the Fort Gibbon military reservation in Alaska, adding a strip along the east side and Bull Island in the Yukon River and turning excluded lands over to the Interior Department.

title: Tucson, Arizona, Office of Gila Land District Transferred to Phoenix
summary: Moved the Gila Land District office from Tucson, Arizona, to Phoenix.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Henry Summers as Clerk in New York Pension Agency Without Examination
summary: Allowed Henry Summers to be appointed a clerk in the New York pension agency without examination.

title: Land Office at Prescott Arizona, Arizona Land District, Abolished; Transferred to Phoenix
summary: Abolished the land office at Prescott in the Arizona Land District and moved its business to Phoenix.

title: Enlargement of the Gila Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Enlarged the Gila River Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, first proclaimed in 1899, to take in more partly timbered public lands, and gave it a new name: the Gila Forest Reserve.

title: Enlargement of the Payson Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Further enlarged the Payson Forest Reserve in Utah, adding partly timbered lands and redrawing its boundaries.

title: Approval of Acting Interior Sec'y's Recommendation of July 18 that Certain Utah Lands Be Added to Uintah Indian Reservation Despite Prior Application for State of Utah for Water Rights from Rock Creek
summary: Added certain Utah lands to the Uintah Indian Reservation on the Acting Interior Secretary's recommendation, despite an earlier application by the State of Utah for water rights from Rock Creek.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Gertrude Weaver as Clerk in Signal Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed temporary clerk Gertrude Weaver to be permanently appointed a clerk in the Signal Service without examination.

title: Approval of Acting Interior Sec'y's Recommendation of July 20 That Additional Lands Within the Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, to Protect Water Rights of the Indians
summary: Added more lands within the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah to protect the Indians' water rights, approving the Acting Interior Secretary's recommendation.

title: Establishment of the Short Pine Forest Reserve, South Dakota
summary: Set aside the Short Pine Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in South Dakota, closed to settlement except for lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Approval of Acting War Secretary's Recommendation of July 21, 1905 Concerning Disposition of Fort Shaw Indian School Reservation, Montana
summary: Approved the Acting Secretary of War's recommendation on what to do with the Fort Shaw Indian School Reservation in Montana.

title: Establishment of the Garden City Forest Reserve, Kansas
summary: Created the Garden City Forest Reserve in western Kansas, reserving public lands from settlement apart from lands already lawfully claimed.

title: Enlargement of the Sierra Forest Reserve, California
summary: Added partly timbered California lands to the Sierra Forest Reserve, using boundary authority Congress extended earlier in 1905 when it moved lands out of Yosemite National Park and into the reserve.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands on Revillagigedo Island, Alaska for Use as a Site for a Lighthouse Depot
summary: Reserved land on Revillagigedo Island, Alaska, as a site for a lighthouse depot.

title: Authorizing Employment of Charles W. Spicer in Bureau of the Census Without Examination
summary: Allowed Charles W. Spicer to be hired without examination in the Bureau of the Census for experimental work on tabulating machines.

title: Approving Acting War Secretary Recommendation of July 28, 1905, to Declare Conveyed Portion of Port Madison Indian Reservation as a Military Reservation
summary: Made lands the government bought from Indians on Agate Passage, once part of the Port Madison Indian Reservation in Washington, into a military reservation for fortifications.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands for the Pueblo Indians of New Mexico Belonging to the Pueblo of Santa Clara
summary: Reserved certain lands for the Pueblo Indians of the Pueblo of Santa Clara in New Mexico.

title: Santa Clara Pueblo Indian Reservation, New Mexico Territory, enlarged, subject to valid existing rights.
Reserving Lands for Town-Site Entries on the Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Reserved tracts in the Uintah Indian Reservation lands of Utah, chosen by the Uintah Allotment Commission and approved by the Interior Department, as sites for future townsites.

title: Ashland and Eau Claire Land Districts, Wis., Abolished; Transferred to Wausau Land District
summary: Abolished the Ashland and Eau Claire land districts in Wisconsin and moved them into the Wausau Land District.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Thomas Harper as a Clerk in the Quartermaster's Department at Large Without Examination
summary: Allowed Thomas Harper to be appointed a clerk in the Quartermaster's Department at large without examination.

title: Modifying Provisions for Opening Lands to Entry on the Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Changed the schedule for the Uintah Indian Reservation land opening so applicants holding drawing numbers 1 to 111, rather than 1 to 50, would be heard each day at the Vernal, Utah, land office starting August 28, 1905.

title: Reserving Lands for Reservoir Site, etc., on Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Withdrew agricultural lands and a reservoir site on the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah from disposal before the opening, to conserve the water supply for the Indians or for general agricultural development.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to March 2, 1906
summary: Extended the deadline for the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to finish its work to March 2, 1906.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Ferdinand Schwarz as an Unclassified Laborer in Government Printing Office
summary: Allowed Ferdinand Schwarz to be appointed permanently as an unclassified laborer in the Government Printing Office.

title: Withdrawal of Lands from Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, for Additional Townsites
summary: Set aside additional lots on the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah as townsites, adding them to the town lands already reserved by a proclamation of July 31, 1905.

title: Reducing Area of Lands Reserved for Reservoir Sites on Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Shrank a reservoir site on the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah to only the lands needed to protect the water supply, returning the rest to their earlier status.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Private Secretary to Purchasing Agent of Post Office Department from Examination
summary: Excepted a private secretary or confidential clerk to the Post Office Department's purchasing agent from civil service examination.

title: Revoking Executive Order of December 9, 1852 Pertaining to Certain Described Lands in Michigan Reserved for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Revoked an 1852 executive order that had reserved certain Michigan lands for lighthouse purposes.

title: Establishment of the Holy Cross Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Created the Holy Cross Forest Reserve on public timberland in Colorado, reserving it from settlement under the 1891 forest reserve law.

title: Santa Barbara Island, Calif., Reserved for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Reserved Santa Barbara Island, California, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Authorizing Appointment of May R. Proctor for a Position in Government Printing Office Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mrs. May R. Proctor to be appointed in the Government Printing Office without examination.

title: Reserving Parcels of Reclaimed Harbor Land, Manila, Philippine Islands, for Military Purposes
summary: Reserved parcels of newly reclaimed harbor land in Manila for military purposes.

title: Excusing Washington Navy Yard Employees From Work on Labor Day, September 4, 1905
summary: Excused Washington Navy Yard employees from work on Labor Day, September 4, 1905.

title: Prescribing Compensation for Members of Advisory Board of Engineers for the Panama Canal
summary: Set pay for each member of the advisory board of engineers on Panama Canal plans: $5,000 on completion of the report, $15 a day in expenses and travel costs, with Generals Davis and Abbott's allowance raised to offset their retired pay.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Philip Cowen as Inspector in the Immigration Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed Philip Cowen to be appointed immigrant inspector in the Immigration Service without a civil service examination.

title: Prescribing Procedure for Removal of Officers and Employees Serving on the Isthmus of Panama
summary: Waived the usual civil service removal procedure for officers and employees on the Isthmus of Panama, while requiring the reasons for removal to be recorded and shared with the Civil Service Commission on request.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands on Gravina and False Islands, Alaska for Light-house Purposes
summary: Reserved land on Gravina and False islands in Alaska for lighthouse purposes.

title: Altering Military Reservation at Fort San Pedro, Iloilo, Panay, Philippine Islands
summary: Redrew the military reservation at Fort San Pedro near Iloilo, Panay, amending a 1903 order so it covers only the public lands within the new bounds.

title: Authorizing Appointment of John B. Goff and D. P. Wells as Assistant Forest Rangers in Forest Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed John B. Goff and D. P. Wells to be appointed assistant forest rangers in the Forest Service without examination.

title: Prescribing Regulations for Presentation of the Congressional Medal of Honor
summary: Required that the Medal of Honor be presented with formal ceremony, by the President or his representative in Washington when practicable; otherwise as the Chief of Staff directs, or by a division or higher commander on campaign.

title: Approving Acting War Secretary Recommendation of September 18, 1905, to Reserve Lands at Safety Harbor and Old Woman, Alaska, for Military Telegraph Purposes
summary: Reserved public lands at Safety Harbor and Old Woman, Alaska, for the Army Signal Corps' military cable and telegraph lines, subject to private rights.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mary E. Enright in Bureau of Engraving and Printing Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Mary E. Enright be reinstated in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing despite the time limit on eligibility for reinstatement.

title: Establishment of the Dixie Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Established the Dixie Forest Reserve on public timberland in Utah, setting it apart from settlement.

title: Authorizing Transfer of W. E. Hall to Clerk in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted W. E. Hall to move from the Isthmian Canal Service to a Class D clerkship in the Treasury Department, waiving civil service Rule X's six-month service requirement.

title: Enlargement of the Madison Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Enlarged the Madison Forest Reserve in Montana, adding public lands partly covered with timber and redrawing its boundaries.

title: Establishment of the Big Belt Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Created the Big Belt Forest Reserve on public timberland in Montana and reserved it from settlement.

title: Establishment of the Shasta Forest Reserve, California
summary: Established the Shasta Forest Reserve on public timberland in California, closing it to settlement.

title: Enlargement and Name Change of Lake Tahoe Forest Reserve, California and Nevada to the Tahoe Forest Reserve
summary: Expanded the Lake Tahoe Forest Reserve with added timberland in California and Nevada and renamed it the Tahoe Forest Reserve.

title: Establishment of the Tonto Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Created the Tonto Forest Reserve on public timberland in the Territory of Arizona and reserved it from settlement.

title: Establishment of the Hell Gate Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Established the Hell Gate Forest Reserve on public timberland in Montana, setting the land aside from settlement.

title: Modifying the Boundaries of the Lincoln Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Redrew the Lincoln Forest Reserve in the Territory of New Mexico, releasing some lands and adding others partly covered with timber; the released lands reopened to settlement.

title: Establishment of the Portales Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Created the Portales Forest Reserve on public land in the Territory of New Mexico and reserved it from settlement.

title: Enlargement of the Little Belt Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Added timbered public lands in Montana to the Little Belt Mountains Forest Reserve, redrew its boundaries and changed its name.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Miss Marjorie H. Young as Clerk in the United States Pension Agency Without Examination Under Civil-Service Rules
summary: Allowed Marjorie H. Young to be kept on and appointed as a clerk in the U.S. pension agency at Pittsburg, Pennsylvania, without a civil service examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mrs. M. C. Miller to a Clerkship in the Classified Service Without Examination Under Civil-Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. M. C. Miller to be appointed to a clerkship in the classified service without a civil service examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Private Secretary to Director of the Geological Survey from Examination
summary: Excepted one private secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey from civil service examination.

title: Abolishing Western Land District, Office at Kingfisher, Oklahoma, and Transferring the Lands, Business, and Archives to Eastern Land District, Office at Guthrie, Oklahoma in Consolidation
summary: Discontinued the western land district in Oklahoma Territory, with its office at Kingfisher, and merged its lands, business and records into the eastern district at Guthrie.

title: Establishing Passage Key Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds
summary: Set aside Passage Key, an island near the mouth of Tampa Bay, Florida, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds under the Department of Agriculture, named the Passage Key Reservation.

title: Establishing Siskiwit Islands Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds
summary: Reserved the Siskiwit (Menagerie) islands off Isle Royal in Lake Superior, Michigan, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, to be called the Siskiwit Islands Reservation.

title: Establishing Huron Islands Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds
summary: Reserved the Huron Islands near Lake Superior's south shore in Michigan as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds under the Department of Agriculture, named the Huron Islands Reservation.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Dessie M. Bowers to Classified Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Dessie M. Bowers of West Virginia be reinstated in any executive department, in view of her earlier service in the Department of Commerce and Labor.

title: Establishment of Jemez Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Established the Jemez Forest Reserve on public lands in the Territory of New Mexico and reserved it from settlement.

title: Forbidding Government Officers and Employees to Assist in Preparation for Civil Service Examinations
summary: Barred federal officers and employees from coaching anyone for Civil Service Commission examinations, making such coaching grounds for removal.

title: Prohibiting the Export of Arms, Ammunition and Munitions of War to the Dominican Republic
summary: Banned the export of arms, ammunition and munitions of war from any port in the United States or Porto Rico to the Dominican Republic until further order.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Dollie A. Slayton as Clerk in Bureau of the Census Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Dollie A. Slayton of Montana, then in a temporary Census Bureau job, to be appointed to the Bureau's permanent clerical roll.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Julia P. Madeira as Bureau of the Census Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Julia P. Madeira of West Virginia, dropped from the Census Bureau during a long illness, be reinstated and transferred to the assayer's office of the mint at Denver.

title: Authorizing Removal of Government Employees for Inefficiency or Incapability Without Trial
summary: Allowed inefficient or incapable classified employees to be removed without a hearing, provided the cause was put in writing, and permitted summary removal for misconduct witnessed by the President or a department head.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles Denby as Chief Clerk of the State Department Without Examination
summary: Allowed Charles Denby to be appointed chief clerk of the State Department without a civil service examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Certain Temporary Workers in Bureau of Fisheries from Examination
summary: Exempted temporary field workers of the Bureau of Fisheries, paid from lump appropriations, from civil service examination.

title: Examinations for Clerical Positions in the Office of the Recorder Of Deeds
summary: Directed the Civil Service Commission to help set up competitive exams, open to District of Columbia residents, for clerical jobs in the Recorder of Deeds office in Washington.

title: Grand Forks Land District, ND, Abolished; Transferred to Devils Lake Land District
summary: Abolished the Grand Forks Land District in North Dakota and moved it into the Devils Lake Land District.

title: Diminishment of Black Hills Forest Reserve, South Dakota - Form of Proclamation
summary: Reduced the Black Hills Forest Reserve in South Dakota, issued in the form of a proclamation.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Edward McCauley as Chief of Redemption Division in Post Office Department Without Examination
summary: Allowed Edward McCauley to be appointed chief of the Post Office Department's Redemption Division without examination, given his experience as chief clerk of the Census Bureau.

title: Thanksgiving Day, 1905
summary: Named Thursday, November 30, 1905, a national day of thanksgiving, giving thanks for bountiful crops and prosperity while urging Americans to own their shortcomings and strive to overcome them.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands in California in Connection With Point Sal Lighthouse Reservation
summary: Reserved additional California lands in connection with the Point Sal lighthouse reservation.

title: Authorizing Additional Compensation for Enlisted Men of the Navy Serving With Submarine Torpedo Boats
summary: Gave qualified Navy enlisted men on submarine torpedo boats $1 extra for each day spent submerged under way, on top of their $5 monthly submarine pay, up to $15 a month.

title: Requiring Examination for Certain Consular Officers in All Consulates General, Consulates, Commercial Agencies, and Consular Agencies
summary: Extended examination requirements to every consulate general, consulate and commercial or consular agency paying at least $1,000 a year, filling vacancies by transfer, promotion, or examination of candidates the President selects.

title: Appointment of Secretaries of Embassy and Legation
summary: Ordered that vacancies for secretaries of embassy or legation be filled by transfer or promotion within the foreign service, or by examination of candidates the President selects.

title: Establishment of the Yuba Forest Reserve, California
summary: Created the Yuba Forest Reserve on public timberland in California and reserved it from settlement.

title: Applying Civil Service Rules or Regulations Regarding Employment of Laborers to Workers at Indian Warehouses
summary: Brought hiring at Indian warehouses under the civil service rules and laborer regulations, giving current employees other than unskilled laborers classified status but requiring an exam before any transfer.

title: Establishing Breton Island Reservation, Louisiana
summary: Set aside Breton Island and the Old Harbor and Freemason islands in Louisiana as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, to be known as the Breton Island Reservation.

title: Approving Acting War Secretary Recommendation of November 13, 1905, to Reserve Lands Near Zamboanga, Mindanao, Philippine Islands, for Target Range
summary: Reserved public land at the western end of the Mesa near Zamboanga, Mindanao, as a target range for the Zamboanga post.

title: Appointments in the Isthmian Canal Service Without Examination in the Absence of Suitably Qualified Eligibles
summary: Let the Civil Service Commission allow temporary Isthmian Canal Service appointments when no eligible with the needed skills is on its registers; these could become permanent on the Canal Commission's certificate.

title: Amending Civil Service Rule XII, Pertaining to Removal
summary: Rewrote civil service Rule XII on removals: like penalties for like offenses, removal only to promote efficiency, written causes, and limits on the Civil Service Commission's power to investigate removals.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Positions Excepted from Examination
summary: Excepted one tobacco examiner and one tea examiner in the Customs Service at Chicago from civil service examination.

title: Bent Land District, Colo., Abolished; Transferred to Valley Land District, Office at Pueblo
summary: Abolished the Bent Land District in Colorado and moved it into the Valley Land District, with its office at Pueblo.

title: Approved Acting Sec'y of War Recommendation of Nov. 20 to Diminish and Transfer Lands of St. Michael Military Reservation to Interior Dept.
summary: Shrank the St. Michael Military Reservation in Alaska and transferred the excluded lands to the Interior Department.

title: Authorizing Appointment of S. H. Alexander as Clerk in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed S. H. Alexander of North Carolina, a classified laborer in the Post Office Department, to be appointed to a permanent clerical position.

title: Amending Executive Order of August 31, 1905, Regarding Compensation for Members of Advisory Board of Engineers for the Panama Canal
summary: Changed one word in the August 31, 1905, pay order for the Panama Canal's Advisory Board of Engineers, from "report" to "work," so foreign members could be paid before heading home.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Marie L. Eastwood in Bureau of the Census Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Marie L. Eastwood to be appointed to a permanent position in the Bureau of the Census, in view of her earlier satisfactory service there.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Cooks from Examination
summary: Excepted cooks from civil service examination when the Commission judges competitive exams impractical.

title: Certain Lands in California Reserved for Lighthouse Purposes (Revoked in Part by EO 5750)
summary: Reserved certain lands in California for lighthouse purposes.

title: Approving War Secretary Recommendation of November 25, 1905, to Reserve Lands at Chilkat Inlet, Alaska, for Water Supply to Fort William H. Seward
summary: Reserved public lands on Chilkat Inlet, Alaska, to supply water to Fort William H. Seward.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Edna M. Peltz as Clerk in Pension Office Without Examination
summary: Allowed Edna M. Peltz to be permanently appointed to a clerical position in the Pension Office without examination.

title: Sidney Land District, Neb., Abolished; Transferred to Western Land District, Office at North Platte
summary: Abolished the Sidney Land District in Nebraska and moved it into the Western Land District at North Platte.

title: Approving War Secretary Recommendation of December 6, 1905, to Reserve Lands at Keystone, Alaska, for Military Telegraph Purposes
summary: Reserved public lands at Keystone, Alaska, for a military telegraph.

title: Authorizing Isthmian Canal Commission to Hold Quarterly Session of January 1, 1906, in Washington, D. C.
summary: Let the Isthmian Canal Commission hold its January 1, 1906, session in Washington instead of on the Isthmus so it could consider the advisory board of engineers' report.

title: Appointing Committee to Plan Inquiry of Government Office Sanitary Conditions for Prevention of Tuberculosis
summary: Answering a National Association for the Study and Prevention of Tuberculosis resolution, appointed the Army, Navy and Public Health surgeons general to plan an inquiry into sanitary conditions in government offices and workshops.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Treasury Department Assistant Assayer Subject to Examination
summary: Made the assistant assayer position in each mint or assay office subject to civil service examination, striking it from the list of excepted positions.

title: Authorizing Reappointment of Emily L. Genella in Bureau of Engraving and Printing Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Emily L. Genella to be reappointed in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing despite the civil service year limit.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Howard H. Belden Upon Passing Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed Howard H. Belden to be appointed in any executive department after passing a noncompetitive examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mary E. Owings to Position in Government Printing Office Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mary E. Owings to be appointed to a position in the Government Printing Office without examination.

title: Classifying Thirteen Special Agents in the Bureau of the Census
summary: Permitted thirteen special agents in the Bureau of the Census to transfer to competitive positions, putting them on the same footing as employees classified by act of Congress.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Katherine S. Todd to Clerk in Office of Commissioner of Internal Revenue Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Katherine S. Todd transfer from the Bureau of Engraving and Printing to a clerkship in the office of the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, waiving civil service Rule X restrictions.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Certain Temporary Positions in Agriculture Department from Examination
summary: Exempted seasonal Agriculture Department guards, guides, cooks, packers, teamsters, choppers and skilled laborers hired during fire season from examination, capping their service at six months a year.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Anna F. McCormick as Clerk in Isthmian Canal Commission Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Anna F. McCormick, temporarily employed by the Isthmian Canal Commission, to be appointed there permanently.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Richard H. Williams as Inspector of Hulls of Steam Vessels Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Richard H. Williams be reinstated as an inspector of hulls of steam vessels despite the one-year limit in the civil service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Nevil Monroe Hopkins as Electrical Engineer in Navy Department After Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed Nevil Monroe Hopkins to be appointed electrical engineer in the Navy's Bureau of Yards and Docks after a noncompetitive examination.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Positions Excepted from Apportionment
summary: Added carpenters, cabinetmakers, painters, plumbers, electricians and related trades to the jobs exempt from the rule apportioning Washington appointments among the states by population, and dropped pages from the list.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Hattie R. McMullin to Position in Interior Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Hattie R. McMullin be reinstated in a classified Interior Department position even though she had been out of the service more than a year.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mrs. Mary E. Griffin in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing Without Regard to Civil-Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. Mary E. Griffin to be reappointed in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing despite the civil service year limit.

title: Temporary appointment of Mrs. Charles (Florence E.) Broady
summary: Made a temporary appointment of Mrs. Charles (Florence E.) Broady.

title: Appointment of Mr. Howard H. Belden
summary: Concerned the appointment of Howard H. Belden.

title: Reciprocal Reduction of Duties with Switzerland
summary: Cut U.S. duties on Swiss argols, brandies, still wines and vermuth, and artworks, matching Switzerland's removal of differential duties on American goods.

title: Stockton Land District, Calif., Abolished; Transferred to Sacramento Land District
summary: Abolished the Stockton Land District in California and moved it into the Sacramento Land District.

title: Creating the Jamestown Tercentennial Commission and Appointing Members Thereto
summary: Created the Jamestown Ter-Centennial Commission, made up of the Secretaries of the Treasury, War and Navy, to carry out the 1905 act for a celebration near Jamestown on Hampton Roads.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except from Examination Stitch Counters in the New York Customs District
summary: Exempted stitch counters in the New York customs district from civil service examination.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Ralph Whitman as Draftsman in Isthmian Canal Commission Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Ralph Whitman, temporarily employed as an engineer draftsman with the Isthmian Canal Commission, to be appointed there permanently.

title: Authorizing Appointment of E. M. LeBoiteaux in Bureau of the Census After Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed E. M. LeBoiteaux to be hired at the Bureau of the Census for experimental work developing tabulating machinery, after a noncompetitive Civil Service Commission examination.

title: Repealing Executive Order No. 370 of November 15, 1905, Regarding Appointments to Isthmian Canal Commission Positions
summary: Repealed the November 15, 1905, executive order governing appointments to Isthmian Canal Commission positions on the Isthmus of Panama.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Positions Excepted from Examination for Isthmian Canal Commission Personnel
summary: Rewrote the civil service exceptions for the Isthmian Canal Commission, exempting all Isthmus jobs except clerks, bookkeepers, stenographers, typists, doctors, trained nurses and draftsmen, and barring noncompetitive appointees from transferring to competitive posts.

title: Reserving Certain Lands in Minnesota for Reservoir System at Mississippi River Headwaters
summary: Withdrew Minnesota lands, including islands in Aitkin, Pokegama and Leyton lakes, from sale for the War Department's reservoir system at the headwaters of the Mississippi River.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Uintah Forest Reserve, Utah and Wyoming
summary: Enlarged the Uintah Forest Reserve, adding lands in Utah and Wyoming and closing them to settlement, apart from valid existing entries.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Walter R. Brinckerhoff as Chief of Leprosy Hospital Station in Hawaii Subject to Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed Dr. Walter R. Brinckerhoff to be appointed head of the leprosy hospital station and laboratory in Hawaii, subject to a noncompetitive examination.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Sevier Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Expanded the Sevier Forest Reserve in Utah, first set apart in May 1905, and reserved the added lands from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Manti Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Extended the boundaries of the Manti Forest Reserve in Utah, established in 1903, closing the added lands to settlement.

title: Reserving Lands at Diamond Head, Kupikipikio Point, and Punchbowl Hill, Hawaii, for Military Purposes
summary: Temporarily withdrew public lands at Diamond Head, Kupikipikio Point and Punchbowl Hill in Hawaii for military use until surveys decide what permanent reservations are needed.

title: Directing Department Heads to Appoint a Committee to Oversee the Printing Requirements and Publications for Each Respective Department
summary: Ordered every executive department to form an advisory committee on printing to cut unnecessary matter, tables and illustrations from reports, and set rules keeping annual reports to concise accounts of work and spending.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Fish Lake Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Enlarged the Fish Lake Forest Reserve in Utah to take in additional lands partly covered with timber.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Jeannette L. Cavanagh as Classified Laborer in Department of Agriculture Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. Jeannette L. Cavanagh to be reinstated as a classified laborer in the Department of Agriculture, by an endorsement on a senator's letter.

title: Authorizing Reappointment of William A. Barr in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted William A. Barr to be reappointed in the Post-Office Department despite the civil-service rules' one-year limit.

title: Prescribing Additional Responsibilities for the United States Board on Geographic Names
summary: Gave the U.S. Board on Geographic Names the job of fixing place names in the United States and its insular possessions, requiring officials to submit new names for approval before publication.

title: Setting Apart the Beaver Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Created the Beaver Forest Reserve on public lands in Utah, reserving them from entry or settlement.

title: Setting Apart the La Sal Forest Reserve, Utah and Colorado
summary: Set apart the La Sal Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in Utah and Colorado, closing them to entry or settlement.

title: Amendment to Executive Order No. 163 of January 31, 1902 to Include Independent Government Agencies
summary: Extended the 1902 order barring federal employees from lobbying Congress for pay raises or other legislation to cover workers in independent government establishments as well as executive departments.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Mounted Inspectors in the Customs Service from Examination
summary: Added mounted customs inspectors on the Mexican border to Schedule A, excepting them from civil-service examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mary H. Donnelly as Clerk in Office of Chief of Ordnance Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mary H. Donnelly to be reinstated as a clerk in the Office of the Chief of Ordnance despite the year limit on reinstatement.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles S. Brown as Inspector in Government Printing Office Subject to Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed Charles S. Brown to be appointed an inspector in the Government Printing Office if he passes a noncompetitive examination.

title: Transferring Certain Lands From Bismarck Land District, N. Dakota to Fargo Land District
summary: Shifted certain lands from the Bismarck Land District to the Fargo Land District in North Dakota.

title: Amending Executive Order of May 21, 1887 to Modify Boundaries of Fort Washakie Military Reservation, Wyoming
summary: Redrew the Fort Washakie military reservation in Wyoming to match a new survey, leaving out land used for Indian school buildings and keeping the Indians' rights to the land.

title: Abolishing Malagi (Malahi) Island Military Reservation, Laguna de Bay, Luzon, Philippine Islands
summary: Abolished the military reservation on Malagi (Malahi) Island in Laguna de Bay, Luzon, as useless, returning it to the Philippine government for the inhabitants' benefit.

title: Reserving Lands and Waters Around Yes Lake, Yes Bay, and Back Bay, Alaska, for Salmon Hatchery
summary: Reserved Yes Lake (Lake McDonald), Yes Bay, Back Bay and strips of shoreline in Alaska as a salmon hatchery site, keeping Native rights to fish and gather fuel.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles H. Ingram as Clerk in War Department Without Examination
summary: Let Charles H. Ingram, who had resigned from the Treasury Department in 1903, take a clerical job in the War Department without examination.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to September 2, 1906
summary: Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission until September 2, 1906, to finish its work.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands in Randlett, Utah, for the Protestant Episcopal Church, for Use and Benefit of Ute Indians
summary: Set aside block 77 in the Randlett, Utah, town site for the Protestant Episcopal Church to use for missionary and cemetery purposes benefiting the Ute Indians.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Clayton G. Coleman as Special Agent in General Land Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Clayton G. Coleman to be reinstated as a special agent of the General Land Office despite the one-year limit in the civil-service rules.

title: Establishing Indian Key Reservation, Tampa Bay, Florida as Preserve and Breeding Ground for Birds
summary: Reserved Indian Key, a ninety-acre island in Tampa Bay, Florida, for the Department of Agriculture as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.

title: Authorizing Appointment of William M. Geddes as Clerk in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted William M. Geddes, longtime disbursing agent for government exhibits at expositions, to become a fourth-class clerk in the Treasury Department without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Promotion of Joseph Fought to Clerk in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Joseph Fought to be promoted from classified laborer to clerk in the Treasury Department, citing his earlier War Department clerkship and gallant Civil War service.

title: Authorizing Appointment of John H. Smith as Laborer in Bureau of Engraving and Printing Without Regard to Laborer Regulations
summary: Allowed John H. Smith to be hired as a laborer in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without following the usual laborer regulations.

title: Clarifying Executive Order No. 348-C of August 31, 1905, Regarding Compensation for Advisory Board of Engineers for the Panama Canal
summary: Rewrote the 1905 order on pay for the Advisory Board of Engineers on Panama Canal plans: $5,000 each on completing the report, $15 a day while working, and travel costs.

title: Boundaries of Bismarck and Fargo Land Districts, N. Dak., Redefined; Certain Lands, With Archives, Records, and Business Pertaining Thereto
summary: Redrew the boundary between the Bismarck and Fargo land districts in North Dakota, moving certain lands along with their records and business.

title: Mangum Land District, Okla., Abolished and Lands, Business, and Archives Transferred to the Lawton Land District
summary: Abolished the Mangum land district in Oklahoma and moved its lands, business and archives to the Lawton land district.

title: Setting Apart the Fruita Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Established the Fruita Forest Reserve on public lands in Colorado and closed them to settlement.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Nine Special Agents in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed nine men who had proved themselves in other posts to be appointed special agents of the Treasury Department without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Prescribing Procedure for Appointment of Laborers Performing Work of Classified Nature
summary: Required laborers who do classified-grade work to be appointed through civil-service certification, and let such laborers already doing that work well be brought into the classified service.

title: Reserving Lands in Unalaklik, Alaska for Use of Army Signal Corps to Operate Military Cable and Telegraph Lines
summary: Reserved public lands at Unalaklik, Alaska, for the Army Signal Corps to operate military cable and telegraph lines.

title: Fixing the Compensation for Members of the Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Set new salaries for the Isthmian Canal Commission, including $30,000 a year for Chairman Theodore P. Shonts and the chief engineer, plus housing and travel allowances.

title: Reciprocal Reduction of Duties with Germany
summary: Lowered U.S. duties on certain German goods, including crude tartar, brandies, still wines and artworks, in return for Germany granting American products its conventional tariff from March 1, 1906.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Katherine Moynihan in Post Office Department Without Examination
summary: Let Mrs. Katherine Moynihan be appointed to a Post-Office Department position without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of James T. Peterson and Clarence W. Allen in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Reinstated James T. Peterson and Clarence W. Allen at the Mobile, Alabama, post office, after the department found they had been unjustly removed.

title: Prescribing Rules for the Prevention of Tuberculosis Among Employees in Public Service
summary: Put a committee's tuberculosis-prevention rules into force across federal offices and workshops, requiring posted rules, examinations of employees suspected of having the disease, and sanitary inspections of public buildings.

title: Amending Consular Regulations, Paragraph 678, Pertaining to Invoices for Exports to the United States
summary: Rewrote a consular regulation so consuls certify invoices for U.S.-bound goods sent by mail or messenger, without requiring shippers to appear in person.

title: Amending Consular Regulations, Paragraph 680, Pertaining to Verification of Invoices
summary: Rewrote a consular regulation directing consuls to check each invoice item, consult chambers of commerce, and, when needed, demand bills of sale, samples or inspection of whole shipments.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Robert Lee Gray as Assistant Messenger in Department of Justice Without Examination
