summary: Allowed Robert Lee Gray to be appointed assistant messenger in the Department of Justice without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Coila B. Ashby as Clerk in Interior Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted Mrs. Coila B. Ashby to be reinstated as a clerk in the Interior Department despite the reinstatement rule's one-year limit.

title: Modifying Boundaries of Fort Egbert Military Reservation, Alaska
summary: Reshaped the Fort Egbert Military Reservation in Alaska, adding public lands and handing a no-longer-useful portion to the Interior Department for disposal.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Gallatin Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Enlarged the Gallatin Forest Reserve in Montana and reserved the added lands from settlement.

title: Admission of J. F. Moreno to Examination for Classified Position Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived the citizenship requirement so J. F. Moreno, a British subject with twelve years in the diplomatic and consular services, could take a civil-service examination.

title: Setting Apart the North Platte Forest Reserve, Nebraska
summary: Created the North Platte Forest Reserve on public lands in Nebraska, closing them to entry and settlement.

title: Reserving Lands on Batan and Cacraray Islands, Philippine Islands, for Military Purposes
summary: Reserved public lands on Batan Island and Cacraray Island in the Philippines for military purposes, including the western part of Batan, about 25 square miles.

title: Setting Apart the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Created the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve in Oregon, absorbing most of the Baker City Forest Reserve, which it replaced; lands left out were restored to the public domain.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands in Alaska for Experimental Agricultural Station
summary: Reserved certain lands in Alaska for an agricultural experiment station.

title: Defining Intention of Order Fixing Salaries and Allowances of Isthmian Canal Commissioners
summary: Clarified that the Isthmian Canal Commission chairman, the Canal Zone governor and the chief engineer are paid actual expenses while traveling on commission business, effective February 26, 1906.

title: Reserving Middle Islands at Rock Harbor, Michigan, for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Set aside the Middle Islands at Rock Harbor, Michigan, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Abolishing Grass Island Military Reservation, Grays Harbor, Washington
summary: Gave up the Grass Island military reservation in Grays Harbor, Washington, placing the island under the Interior Department since it was not needed for defense.

title: Boundaries of Billings Land District, Montana, Redefined
summary: Redefined the boundaries of the Billings land district in Montana.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Pyeng E. Yoon as Clerk in Post Office at Honolulu Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Waived the citizenship rule so Pyeng E. Yoon, a Korean subject, could be a Korean-speaking clerk in the Honolulu post office after an examination found no eligible candidates.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles P. Galpin as Classified Laborer in Bureau of Pensions Without Examination
summary: Let Charles P. Galpin be appointed a classified laborer in the Bureau of Pensions without examination.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Joseph F. Laporte to Post Office Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Joseph F. Laporte to be reinstated in the post-office service despite the time limit on reinstatement.

title: Authorizing Employment of Jacob S. McClure in Classified Service
summary: Let Jacob S. McClure, a Civil War veteran whose laborer job at the Topeka pension agency was abolished, be reemployed in a classified position.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Benjamin B. Cox to Post Office Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Benjamin B. Cox to be reinstated at the Mobile, Alabama, post office without regard to civil-service Rule IX.

title: Setting Apart the Helena Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Set apart the Helena Forest Reserve on public lands in Montana, closing them to entry and settlement.

title: Reserving Lands in Mississippi as Target Range for Revenue Cutter Service
summary: Reserved two sections of land in Mississippi, 307.54 acres in all, as a target range for the Revenue-Cutter Service.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Harry H. Brewster to Finance Clerk in Post Office Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Harry H. Brewster to move from the unclassified South St. Joseph post office to finance clerk at the St. Joseph, Missouri, post office without meeting civil-service requirements.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mary A. McDonald as Clerk in Department of the Interior Without Examination
summary: Permitted Mrs. Mary A. McDonald to be appointed a clerk in the Department of the Interior without examination.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Ashland Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Enlarged the Ashland Forest Reserve in Oregon, first established in 1893, and reserved the added lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Vernon Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Established the Vernon Forest Reserve on public lands in Utah.

title: Abolishing the Office of Surveyor General for Florida
summary: Abolished the office of Surveyor General for Florida.

title: Land Office at San Francisco, Calif., Ordered Temporarily Removed to Oakland
summary: Temporarily moved the San Francisco land office to Oakland, California, after the 1906 earthquake and fire.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of George M. Shafer as Watchman in Department of the Interior Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed George M. Shafer, a Civil War veteran, to be permanently appointed a watchman in the Department of the Interior without meeting civil-service requirements.

title: Setting Apart the Ruby Mountains Forest Reserve, Nevada
summary: Created the Ruby Mountains Forest Reserve on public lands in Nevada.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Weiser Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Enlarged the Weiser Forest Reserve in Idaho, established in May 1905, and closed the added lands to settlement.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands in Juneau, Alaska, for Educational Purposes
summary: Reserved certain lands in Juneau, Alaska, for educational purposes.

title: Revoking Executive Order No. 372-A of November 18, 1905, Abolishing Bent Land District, Colorado, with Office at Lamar
summary: Revoked the November 1905 order abolishing the Bent land district in Colorado, keeping the district and its office at Lamar.

title: Maj. Gen. F.C. Ainsworth, Military Sec'y, and Brig. Gen. J. Franklin Bell Designated to Act, In the Order Named, as War Sec'y During the Absence
summary: Designated Maj. Gen. F. C. Ainsworth and Brig. Gen. J. Franklin Bell, in that order, to act as Secretary of War during the Secretary's absence.

title: Setting Apart the Fillmore Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Set apart the Fillmore Forest Reserve on public lands in Utah.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Harry E. Burns as Fireman Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Harry E. Burns, honorably discharged as a Navy fireman, to be appointed fireman in any department at Washington.

title: Transferring Certain Specified Archives of the Department of State to the Library of Congress
summary: Transferred historical archives from the State Department to the Library of Congress, including Revolutionary-era orderly books, Albert Gallatin's Treasury correspondence, Burr Conspiracy papers and Jefferson Davis papers.

title: Opening of the Ceded Portion of the Crow Indian Reservation, Montana
summary: Opened the ceded, unallotted lands of the Crow Indian Reservation in Montana to settlement and entry under the homestead, town-site and mineral land laws.

title: Authorizing Appointment of O. Louis Cleven to Bureau of the Census After Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Allowed O. Louis Cleven to be appointed in the Bureau of the Census for experimental work on tabulating machinery, subject to a noncompetitive examination.

title: Inviting the Militia to Attend the Jamestown, Virginia Tercentennial Celebration
summary: Invited state and territorial governors to send militia, at their own expense, to the Jamestown tercentennial celebration on Hampton Roads, Virginia.

title: Setting Apart the Bear River Forest Reserve, Idaho and Utah
summary: Created the Bear River Forest Reserve on public lands in Idaho and Utah, in place of the Logan Forest Reserve.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Wichita Forest Reserve, Oklahoma
summary: Enlarged the Wichita Forest Reserve in Oklahoma Territory, established in 1901, and reserved the added lands from settlement.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Uinta Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Trimmed the Uinta Forest Reserve, releasing certain lands in Utah and Wyoming and opening them to settlement, with entry allowed after ninety days' notice.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mrs. M. C. Kratz to Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. M. C. Kratz to be reinstated in the Treasury Department, since she had been removed through inadvertence.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Clerks on Isthmus of Panama Earning Less than $75 Monthly Without Examination
summary: Exempted clerical jobs on the Isthmus of Panama paying under $75 a month from civil-service examination and eased transfers and promotions among classified positions there.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Hell Gate Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Enlarged the Hell Gate Forest Reserve in Montana, created in October 1905, closing the added lands to settlement.

title: Opening of the Wind River Indian Reservation in Wyoming
summary: Opened the unallotted lands ceded by the Shoshone and Arapahoe tribes on the Shoshone or Wind River Reservation in Wyoming to settlement under the homestead, townsite, coal and mineral land laws.

title: Opening for Location Mineral Lands in the Uncompahgre Indian Reservation, Utah
summary: Dealt with gilsonite, asphaltum and elaterite lands in the former Uncompahgre Indian Reservation in Utah, upholding mining claims recorded before 1891 and providing for sale of the remaining mineral lands.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Jesse F. Gates as Classified Laborer in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Jesse F. Gates, severely wounded in the Spanish war, to be reinstated as a classified laborer in the Treasury Department.

title: Transferring Certain Described Lands in Oklahoma Known as the “Government Acre” from the Interior Dept. to the Treasury Dept. for Post Office and Other Government Purposes
summary: Transferred the "Government Acre" in Oklahoma from the Interior Department to the Treasury Department for a post office and other government purposes.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands Within the Salt Lake Forest Reserve, Utah, for Use as a Nursery Site
summary: Reserved certain lands inside the Salt Lake Forest Reserve in Utah as a nursery site.

title: Modifying Fort. St. Michael Military Reservation, Alaska
summary: Amended a 1905 order on Fort St. Michael, Alaska, so that all reservation land except a described military tract would pass to the Interior Department for disposal, effective November 1, 1907.

title: Officer in Charge of Public Buildings and Grounds Authorized to Employ A Copyist For Up to Three Months in Connection With the Inventory
summary: Let the officer in charge of Public Buildings and Grounds hire a copyist for up to three months to help with an inventory.

title: Authorizing Civil Service Commission to Certify Non-Citizens for Appointment Under Certain Prescribed Conditions
summary: Allowed the Civil Service Commission, when too few American citizens qualified for posts such as interpreter, to accept non-citizen applicants, certifying them only when no eligible citizens remained.

title: Amending Executive Order No. 442 of April 27, 1906, Abolishing the Office of Surveyor General for Florida, to Make the Effective Date of Such Abolition June 30, 1907 Instead of June 30, 1906
summary: Pushed back the abolition of the Surveyor General's office for Florida, ordered in April 1906, from June 30, 1906, to June 30, 1907.

title: Excluding Lands Reserved for Town Sites in the Hailey Land District, Idaho
summary: Removed certain tracts from a 1904 land withdrawal in the Hailey Land District, Idaho, so they could be used for town sites under an April 1906 act.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Cressy L. Wilbur to Chief Statistician in Bureau of the Census Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Cleared the way for Dr. Cressy L. Wilbur, an expert special agent, to move up to chief statistician for vital statistics at the Bureau of the Census.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Remove Six Month Limitation on Temporary Forest Guards
summary: Changed the civil-service rules so temporary forest guards, unlike other seasonal fire-season workers, were no longer limited to six months of work a year.

title: Ordering Four Hour Workdays on Saturdays During Summer for Washington Navy Yard Workers
summary: Made Saturdays in July, August and September four-hour workdays for mechanics, laborers and classified employees at the Washington navy yard, with time-and-a-half for extra hours.

title: Reserving Certain Land Within the Belle Fourche Irrigation Project, S. Dak., for Agricultural Experimental Work
summary: Reserved land within the Belle Fourche irrigation project in South Dakota for agricultural experiment work.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Certain Positions in Fifth Internal Revenue District of North Carolina Subject to Examination
summary: Required civil-service examinations for certain internal revenue positions in North Carolina's fifth district that were exempt elsewhere.

title: All Unappropriated Public Lands in the Wausau Land District, Wisconsin, North of Township 33, Withdrawn from Entry, Settlement or Other Appropriation for 90 Days
summary: Withdrew the unappropriated public lands in Wisconsin's Wausau land district north of Township 33 from entry, settlement or other claims for 90 days.

title: Ordering Four Hour Workdays on Saturdays During Summer for Government Printing Office Workers
summary: Set four-hour Saturdays for skilled mechanics, laborers and classified workers at the Government Printing Office in July, August and September, paying time-and-a-half for longer shifts.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Everett J. Dallas to Competitive Position in Interior Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Everett J. Dallas, a Civil War veteran, move from an "additional" seat on the board of pension appeals to a regular, competitive seat as the extra posts were cut.

title: Col. O. H. Ernst Ordered to Continue as Member of International Water Ways Commission
summary: Kept Col. O. H. Ernst on as a member of the International Waterways Commission.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Lincoln Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Enlarged the Lincoln Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory to take in additional land partly covered with timber.

title: Setting Apart the San Luis Obispo Forest Reserve, California
summary: Created the San Luis Obispo Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in California.

title: Setting Apart the Monterey Forest Reserve, California
summary: Established the Monterey Forest Reserve from partly timbered public lands in California.

title: Ordering Four Hour Workdays on Saturdays During Summer for Navy Yard and Naval Station Workers
summary: Extended summer four-hour Saturdays to skilled mechanics, laborers and classified employees at every U.S. navy yard and naval station, with time-and-a-half for extra hours.

title: Regulations Governing Consular Appointments and Promotions
summary: Set merit rules for the newly reorganized consular service: top consular posts filled by promotion for ability and efficiency, and entry-level consul posts by promotion or by examination.

title: Ordering Four Hour Workdays on Saturdays During Summer for War Department and Army Headquarters Workers
summary: Gave War Department arsenal, depot and Army headquarters workers four-hour Saturdays during July, August and September.

title: Authorizing Temporary Appointment of Pension Examiner Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted one more special pension examiner to be hired for six months outside the civil-service rules, on top of five already excepted.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Emma King to Bureau of Engraving and Printing Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mrs. Emma King (née Anderson) to return to the Bureau of Engraving and Printing even though more than a year had passed since she left.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James K. Dawes as Clerk in Post Office at Philadelphia Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Appointed James K. Dawes a clerk at $1,200 a year in the Philadelphia post office, waiving the usual civil-service eligibility rules.

title: Enlargement of the Black Mesa Forest Reserve, Territory of Arizona
summary: Expanded the Black Mesa Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory by changing its boundaries to add land.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Charles N. Twadell to Competitive Position in Bureau of Pensions Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Moved Charles N. Twadell from an exam-exempt special examiner job in the Bureau of Pensions to a similar post under the regular rules.

title: Fixing Compensation for Members of the Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Fixed salaries for the Isthmian Canal Commission, from $30,000 for Chairman Theodore P. Shonts to $7,500 for three commissioners, and set rules for housing and travel expenses.

title: Ordering Preference for Military Veterans for Appointment to Certain Positions in State, War, and Navy Department Building
summary: Directed the Civil Service Commission to give honorably discharged Navy and military men preference for fireman, engineer and similar jobs in the State, War, and Navy Department building.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Ralph Modjeski as Consulting Engineer in Ordnance Department After Noncompetitive Examination
summary: Let Ralph Modjeski be appointed consulting engineer at Rock Island Arsenal, after a noncompetitive exam, while the Rock Island bridge and viaduct were built.

title: Modifying Fort Bayard Military Reservation, New Mexico
summary: Redrew the boundaries of the Fort Bayard military reservation in New Mexico to match General Land Office plats, adding a narrow strip of public land on the west side.

title: Authorizing Appointment of William E. DeRiemer as Clerk in Smithsonian Institution Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed William E. De Riemer, who had spent about seven years on National Museum exposition work, to be hired as a Smithsonian clerk at up to $900 a year.

title: Smithsonian Institution Employees Working on International Catalogue of Scientific Literature Classified Under Civil Service Rules
summary: Brought four Smithsonian employees working on the International Catalogue of Scientific Literature into the classified service, with future hires for that work made under civil-service rules.

title: Classifying Certain Laborers in the Bureau of Fisheries
summary: Classified Bureau of Fisheries field laborers doing fish-culture work, letting them be transferred and promoted under civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Clerks on Isthmus of Panama Earning Less than $75 Monthly Erroneously Appointed under Executive Order No. 394 of January 12, 1906
summary: Allowed clerical jobs on the Isthmus of Panama paying $75 a month or less to be filled without examination, and let clerks hired by mistake under a January 1906 order become permanent.

title: Setting Apart the Pinnacles Forest Reserve, California
summary: Set apart the Pinnacles Forest Reserve on public lands in California.

title: Setting Apart the Heppner Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Created the Heppner Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon.

title: Directing Entries on Shoshone Reservation, Wyoming, to be Made at Shoshoni, Wyoming
summary: Ordered that applications to enter newly opened Shoshone (Wind River) Reservation lands be filed at Shoshoni, Wyoming, instead of Lander, through October 3, 1906.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Michael J. Holland as Clerk in Marine Corps Headquarters Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Michael J. Holland, an enlisted Marine, be appointed a clerk at Marine Corps headquarters.

title: Removing Lands from Malabang Military Reservation, Mindanao, Philippine Islands, for Use by Town of Malabang
summary: Cut land out of the Malabang military reservation on Mindanao, Philippine Islands, for the newly organized municipality of Malabang.

title: Trust period on certain Oklahoma lands allotted to Sac, Fox and Iowa Indians extended ten years.
summary: Extended by ten years the trust period on certain Oklahoma lands allotted to Sac and Fox and Iowa Indians.

title: Ordering Four Hour Workdays on Saturdays During Summer for Engineer Department at Large Workers of the War Department
summary: Set four-hour Saturdays in July, August and September for mechanics, laborers and other workers in the War Department's Engineer Department at Large.

title: Granting Saturday Half Holidays in July, August and September to Workers at Office of Public Buildings and Grounds
summary: Granted Office of Public Buildings and Grounds employees, except the Park Police, paid Saturday half-holidays in July, August and September, with conditions for temporary workers.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Elizabeth Stack as Clerk in Pension Office Without Examination
summary: Permitted Miss Elizabeth Stack to be appointed to a clerical job in the Pension Office without a civil-service exam.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands in California, Previously Reserved for Military Purposes, for Naval Purposes
summary: Turned certain California lands, previously reserved for military use, over to naval purposes.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Tony Verrosso as Unclassified Laborer Without Regard to Laborer Regulations
summary: Let Tony Verrosso, a Spanish-American War veteran, be hired as an unclassified laborer out of the usual certification order.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Florence E. Broady in Government Printing Office Without Examination
summary: Allowed Mrs. Florence E. Broady a permanent Government Printing Office appointment without a civil-service exam.

title: Portion of El Reno Land District, Oklahoma, Transferred to Lawton Land District
summary: Moved part of the El Reno Land District in Oklahoma into the Lawton Land District.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Julia Lynah McCoy in Treasury Department Without Examination
summary: Authorized Mrs. Julia Lynah McCoy's appointment to a Treasury Department position without a civil-service exam.

title: Modifying Boundaries of Grand Canyon Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Redrew the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, adding some timbered land, dropping other tracts and restoring those to settlement.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to January 1, 1907
summary: Extended the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission's authority to January 1, 1907, and no longer, so it could finish judging U.S. citizens' claims against Spain.

title: Setting Apart the Crazy Mountains Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Set apart the Crazy Mountains Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Montana.

title: Changing Title of Board on Geographic Names to United States Geographic Board, and Adding Duties
summary: Renamed the Board on Geographic Names the United States Geographic Board and gave it advisory power over federal mapmaking, including avoiding duplicate work and standardizing scales and symbols.

title: Setting Apart the Kootenai Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Established the Kootenai Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in Montana.

title: Headquarters of Coeur d'Alene Indian Agency Moved to Tekoa
summary: Moved the headquarters of the Coeur d'Alene Indian Agency to Tekoa.

title: Amending Consular Regulations
summary: Amended the regulations governing the U.S. consular service.

title: Prescribing Tariff of Consular Fees, Effective November 1, 1906
summary: Set a new tariff of fees for U.S. consular services, effective November 1, 1906, payable in gold, with American vessels and seamen exempt by law.

title: Authorizing Appointment of W. M. Johnson as Clerk in Immigration Service Without Examination
summary: Let W. M. Johnson be appointed in the Immigration Service without a civil-service exam.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of E. J. Mooklar as Clerk in Naval Station at Tutuila, Samoa Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed E. J. Mooklar to be reinstated as clerk to the commandant of the naval station at Tutuila, Samoa, despite the one-year reinstatement limit.

title: Setting Apart the Wasatch Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Created the Wasatch Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Utah.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Everett Spring in Bureau of the Census Without Examination
summary: Let Everett Spring join the Bureau of the Census without an exam, based on his earlier work as a census clerk and local special agent.

title: Setting Apart the Goose Lake Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Set apart the Goose Lake Forest Reserve on public lands in Oregon.

title: Asking Aid to Valparaiso Earthquake Sufferers
summary: Called on Americans to help the earthquake victims of Valparaiso, Chile, recalling the world's help to San Francisco that spring, and pointed donors to the National Red Cross.

title: Reciprocity with Spain
summary: Lowered U.S. duties on certain Spanish products after Spain gave American goods its minimum tariff rates starting September 1, 1906.

title: Trust period on certain Oklahoma lands allotted to Sac, Fox and Iowa Indians extended ten years.
summary: Extended for ten years the trust period on certain Oklahoma lands allotted to Sac and Fox and Iowa Indians.

title: Washington Navy Yard Employees Excused from Work on Labor Day, Sept. 3
summary: Excused Washington Navy Yard employees from work on Labor Day, September 3, 1906.

title: Restoring Parcel of Land in Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, to Public Domain
summary: Restored two small lots in the former Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, to the public domain after they were mistakenly included in David Eskelson's homestead.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Stanislaus Forest Reserve, California
summary: Added partly timbered land in California to the Stanislaus Forest Reserve.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Alice A. Masters as Clerk in Bureau of the Census Without Examination
summary: Permitted Miss Alice A. Masters to be appointed a Census Bureau clerk without a civil-service exam.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Hell Gate Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Further enlarged the Hell Gate Forest Reserve in Montana with additional partly timbered land.

title: Removing Lands from Fort Robinson Military Reservation, Nebraska
summary: Handed part of the Fort Robinson military reservation, Nebraska, to the Interior Department for disposal, since it was useless for military purposes and had been mistakenly included in private patents.

title: Reciprocity with Bulgaria
summary: Reduced U.S. duties on certain Bulgarian goods after Bulgaria granted American products its lowest conventional tariff rates.

title: Setting Apart the Fremont Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Set apart the Fremont Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon.

title: Consolidating the Yuba Forest Reserve with the Tahoe Forest Reserve, California and Nevada
summary: Combined the Tahoe and Yuba forest reserves, with added land, into a single Tahoe Forest Reserve in California and Nevada.

title: Authorizing Extra Compensation for Enlisted Men in Marine Corps Detailed as Messmen
summary: Authorized extra pay for enlisted Marines detailed as messmen.

title: Opening to Settlement Certain Lands in the Kiowa, Comanche and Apache Indian Reservations
summary: Opened to settlement the 480,000 acres of grazing land and the wood reserve in the Kiowa, Comanche and Apache reservations, Oklahoma Territory, except tracts allotted, sold or set aside for town sites.

title: Requiring Executive Departments to Report Instances of Supervised Contractors Working in Excess of Eight Hours in a Day
summary: Told federal departments overseeing public works to report every case of contractors working laborers or mechanics more than eight hours in a day.

title: Setting Apart the Lolo Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Created the Lolo Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Montana.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Julius H. Hammond, Clerk in General Land Office, to Competitive Service
summary: Moved Julius H. Hammond, a General Land Office depositary and confidential clerk, into the competitive classified service along with his position.

title: Authorizing Isthmian Canal Commission to Hold Next Quarterly Session on November 15, 1906, Instead of October 1, 1906, on the Isthmus of Panama
summary: Rescheduled the Isthmian Canal Commission's quarterly session from October 1 to November 15, 1906, at the Canal Zone governor's office in Panama.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Shasta Forest Reserve, California
summary: Enlarged the Shasta Forest Reserve in California with additional partly timbered land.

title: Setting Apart the Long Pine Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Set apart the Long Pine Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Montana.

title: Setting Aside Devils Tower National Monument, Wyoming
summary: Declared Devils Tower in Crook County, Wyoming, a national monument under the new Antiquities Act, calling the lofty, isolated rock "a natural wonder" and warning against injuring it.

title: Opening to Settlement Lands Within the Walker River Indian Reservation
summary: Opened unallotted, unreserved lands of the Walker River Indian Reservation in Nevada, ceded by the Pah Ute Indians, to settlement at noon on October 29, 1906.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Joseph Tyssowski in Interior Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Joseph Tyssowski, valued for his knowledge of public land law, to be reinstated in the Interior Department despite the time limit.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Except Private Secretary in Customs Office at Port of New York from Examination
summary: Exempted one private secretary in the naval officer of customs' office at the port of New York from civil-service examination.

title: Authorizing Prizes for Excellence in Gunnery Exercises and Target Practice for Men of Marine Corps
summary: Extended Navy prizes for excellence in gunnery and target practice, afloat and ashore, to enlisted Marines on the same terms, for competitions after June 30, 1906.

title: Approving Removal of Office of Surveyor General of Alaska from Sitka to Juneau
summary: Approved moving the Surveyor General of Alaska's office from Sitka to Juneau.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Santa Barbara Forest Reserve, California
summary: Expanded the Santa Barbara Forest Reserve in California to take in additional partly timbered land.

title: Excusing United States Spanish War Veterans Federal Employees in Washington from Work for Spanish War Veterans' Parade
summary: Gave members of the United Spanish War Veterans working in Washington's federal departments, printing office and navy yard the day off October 9, 1906, to march in the group's parade.

title: Removing Lands from Fort San Pedro Military Reservation, Iloilo, Panay, Philippine Islands, for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Carved the Iloilo port light site, mistakenly included in the Fort San Pedro military reservation on Panay, Philippine Islands, out of that reservation.

title: Setting Apart the Siskiyou Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Created the Siskiyou Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in Oregon.

title: Setting Apart the Mount Taylor Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Set apart the Mount Taylor Forest Reserve on partly timbered public lands in New Mexico Territory.

title: Authorizing Retention of Joe Osscar as Engineer in Leech Lake Indian Agency Without Examination
summary: Let Joe Osscar stay on as engineer at the Leech Lake Indian Agency in Minnesota without a civil-service exam.

title: Excusing Members of the Grand Army of the Republic Employed in Executive Departments at Washington from Duty for Spanish War Veterans' Parade
summary: Excused members of the Grand Army of the Republic working in the executive departments at Washington from duty for the Spanish War Veterans' parade.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Uinta Forest Reserve, Utah and Wyoming
summary: Added more partly timbered land in Utah to the Uinta Forest Reserve, which spans Utah and Wyoming.

title: Including Portion of Fort Grant Military Reservation, Arizona, in Mt. Graham Forest Reserve
summary: Made part of the Fort Grant military reservation in Arizona part of the Mt. Graham Forest Reserve, while keeping it open to unhampered War Department use and closed to land-law claims.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission Until March 2, 1907
summary: Extended the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission's powers to examine and settle U.S. citizens' claims against Spain until March 2, 1907.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Diamond Mountain Forest Reserve, California
summary: Enlarged the Diamond Mountain Forest Reserve, first proclaimed July 14, 1905, by adding partly timbered lands in California and reserving them from settlement.

title: Prescribing Regulations Governing the Presentation of the Medal of Honor to Navy Enlisted Men and Officers
summary: Set the ceremony for presenting the Medal of Honor to Navy enlisted men and officers, with recipients ordered to Washington, when practicable, to receive it from the President or his representative.

title: Thanksgiving Day, 1906
summary: Proclaimed Thursday, November 29, 1906, a day of national thanksgiving and prayer for the year's blessings.

title: Administration of Provisional Government of Cuba through the Bureau of Insular Affairs
summary: Directed that Cuba's temporary government be run in Havana by the Provisional Governor under the Secretary of War, with related business in the United States handled by the War Department's Bureau of Insular Affairs.

title: Reserving Abandoned Portion of New Fort Lyon Military Reservation, Bent County, Colorado, and Buildings Thereon, for the Navy Department for Sanitarium Purposes
summary: Set aside the abandoned part of the New Fort Lyon Military Reservation in Bent County, Colorado, and its buildings for the Navy Department to use as a sanitarium.

title: Reserving Lands Near Valdez, Alaska, as Target Range for Fort Liscum
summary: Reserved a tract on the glacial flats of Valdez Glacier, north of the town of Valdez, Alaska, as a target range for the troops of Fort Liscum.

title: Authorizing Promotion of Paul A. Hines Without Examination
summary: Allowed Paul A. Hines, a clerk in the office of the Secretary of Agriculture, to be promoted without a civil-service examination.

title: Setting Apart the Sierra Madre Forest Reserve, Wyoming
summary: Created the Sierra Madre Forest Reserve in Wyoming, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Gallinas Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Established the Gallinas Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Chiricahua Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Enlarged the Chiricahua Forest Reserve, first proclaimed July 30, 1902, by adding partly timbered lands in Arizona Territory and reserving them from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Magdalena Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Set apart the Magdalena Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the San Mateo Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Created the San Mateo Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Peloncillo Forest Preserve, New Mexico
summary: Established the Peloncillo Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Lemhi Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Set apart the Lemhi Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Raft River Forest Reserve, Idaho and Utah
summary: Created the Raft River Forest Reserve, spanning Idaho and Utah, and reserved the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Snowy Mountains Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Established the Snowy Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Ekalaka Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Set apart the Ekalaka Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Big Hole Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Created the Big Hole Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Kootenai Forest Reserve, Montana and Idaho
summary: Enlarged the Kootenai Forest Reserve in Montana, proclaimed August 13, 1906, by adding partly timbered lands across the line in Idaho.

title: Setting Apart the Charleston Forest Reserve, Nevada
summary: Established the Charleston Forest Reserve in Nevada, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Independence Forest Reserve, Nevada
summary: Set apart the Independence Forest Reserve in Nevada, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Baboquivari Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Created the Baboquivari Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Salmon River Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Established the Salmon River Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Abolishing Marshall Land District, Minnesota, with Office at St. Cloud, and Lands and Business Transferred to Duluth Land District
summary: Abolished the Marshall Land District in Minnesota, whose office was at St. Cloud, and moved its lands and business to the Duluth Land District.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Albert M. West as Scientific Assistant in Department of Agriculture Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted Albert M. West of Massachusetts to be reinstated as a scientific assistant in the Department of Agriculture despite the one-year limit of civil-service Rule IX, citing his unusual, expert qualifications.

title: Setting Apart the Huachuca Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Set apart the Huachuca Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Coeur d'Alene Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Created the Coeur d'Alene Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Priest River Forest Reserve, Idaho and Washington
summary: Added partly timbered lands in Idaho to the Priest River Forest Reserve of Idaho and Washington, first proclaimed February 22, 1897.

title: Setting Apart the Manzano Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Established the Manzano Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Pryor Mountains Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Set apart the Pryor Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Missoula Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Created the Missoula Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Little Belt Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Redrew the Little Belt Forest Reserve in Montana, adding partly timbered lands and excluding others; the excluded lands returned to the public domain and opened to settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Lolo Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Enlarged the Lolo Forest Reserve, first proclaimed September 20, 1906, by adding partly timbered lands in Montana and reserving them from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Sawtooth Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Enlarged the Sawtooth Forest Reserve, first proclaimed May 29, 1905, by adding partly timbered lands in Idaho and reserving them from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Jemez Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Enlarged the Jemez Forest Reserve, first proclaimed October 12, 1905, by adding partly timbered lands in New Mexico Territory and reserving them from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Taos Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Established the Taos Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Tumacacori Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Created the Tumacacori Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules to Make Deputy Collectors in Internal Revenue Service Subject to Examination
summary: Struck deputy collectors of internal revenue from the civil-service list of positions excepted from examination, bringing them under the examination requirement.

title: Amending the Organization and Duties of the Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Reorganized the Isthmian Canal Commission: set quarterly sessions on the Isthmus, a four-member quorum, and its duties for building the canal, abolished its Executive Committee, and created an organization of the Chairman and department heads.

title: Reserving Portion of Cape Hinchinbrook, Hinchinbrook Island, Alaska, for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Reserved part of Cape Hinchinbrook on Hinchinbrook Island, Alaska, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Ordering Pay Increases for Navy Men Serving More than One Enlistment and Instructors of Apprentice Seamen
summary: Raised Navy pay $5 a month for men in their second enlistment and $3 more for each later one, and added special-duty pay for petty officers and apprentices who instruct apprentice seamen.

title: Setting Aside Game Preserve in Grand Canyon Forest Reserve, Arizona
summary: Designated the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve lands north and west of the Colorado River in Arizona Territory as a game preserve and breeding ground, making hunting or trapping game there unlawful except under Agriculture Department rules.

title: Prescribing Rules Governing Peacetime Purchase of Discharge from the Navy
summary: Set rules letting Navy enlisted men in their first enlistment buy their discharge in peacetime after one year, with the price tied to outfit cost and months served, and relief for men supporting destitute relatives.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Theodore C. M. Schindler as Special Agent in Bureau of Corporations Without Examination
summary: Let Theodore C. M. Schindler be appointed a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations without a civil-service examination.

title: Setting Aside El Morro National Monument, New Mexico
summary: Proclaimed El Morro National Monument in New Mexico Territory, protecting the rocks known as El Morro and Inscription Rock, judged "of the greatest historical value," and warning against injuring them or settling the land.

title: Setting Aside Montezuma Castle National Monument, Arizona
summary: Proclaimed Montezuma Castle National Monument in Arizona Territory, reserving the prehistoric structure known as Montezuma's Castle and surrounding land for its protection.

title: Setting Aside Petrified Forest National Monument, Arizona
summary: Created Petrified Forest National Monument to protect the fossilized wood of the "Petrified Forest" in Gila and Apache counties, Arizona Territory, warning against excavating, injuring or destroying the deposits.

title: Authorizing Appointment of William W. Gillespie as Deputy Collector in Customs Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed William W. Gillespie to be appointed deputy collector in the Customs Service at Stamford, Connecticut, without examination.

title: Reserving Island Known as “Rock of Ages” in Lake Superior, Michigan for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Reserved the island called Rock of Ages in Lake Superior, Michigan, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Alfred W. Brown in Customs Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted Alfred W. Brown, former appraiser of merchandise at the port of Boston, to be reinstated in the classified Customs Service there without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Amending Consular Service Regulation of June 27, 1906, Governing Appointment and Promotion in the Consular Service
summary: Amended the June 27, 1906, Consular Service regulation so student interpreters are treated like vice consuls, deputy consuls and consular agents for appointment and promotion.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Three Watchmen in Department of the Interior Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let three Civil War veterans serving as temporary watchmen in the Interior Department — Philip M. Earle, Isaac Pearson and George F. Miller — be appointed permanently without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Kate S. Jones to Clerk in Department of the Interior Without Examination
summary: Allowed Kate Jones of Tennessee to move from classified laborer in the Patent Office to clerk at the Knoxville pension agency without examination.

title: Removing Lands from Fort Davis Military Reservation, Texas
summary: Turned about 300 acres of the Fort Davis Military Reservation in Presidio County, Texas, no longer useful for military purposes, over to the Secretary of the Interior.

title: Reserving Certain Described Lands in New Mexico for the Use and Benefit of the Indians of the Jemez Pueblo
summary: Withdrew public lands in township 16 north, range 1 east, New Mexico, from sale and settlement and set them apart for the Indians of the Jemez Pueblo.

title: Amending Tariff of Consular Fees to Exempt Affidavit Fees for Owners of Sealskin Garments Entering from Canada
summary: Amended the consular fee schedule so owners of sealskin garments entering the United States from Canada pay no fee for an affidavit of temporary stay.

title: Authorizing Transfer of William A. Woodruff to Clerk in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed William A. Woodruff, a hospital attendant at Ellis Island, to transfer to a Treasury Department clerical job in Washington without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Transfer of W. B. Johnson to Clerk in Department of the Interior Without Examination
summary: Let W. B. Johnson, a Government Printing Office compositor, transfer without examination to clerk in the Interior Department's Land Service.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Joseph J. Harvey to Subclerical Position in Civil Service
summary: Allowed Joseph J. Harvey, a messenger at the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission, to be transferred or appointed to any other subclerical civil-service position.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Henry G. Balkam to Clerk in Bureau of the Census Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Changed Henry G. Balkam's status from skilled laborer to clerk in the Bureau of the Census, citing his valuable service and a coming cut in the laborer force.

title: Revoking the Military Reservation of Camp Hartshorne in the Philippine Islands
summary: Revoked the Camp Hartshorne military reservation on Laguan Island, Samar, Philippines, returning the land to the Philippine government for the benefit of its inhabitants.

title: Prescribing Official Manner of Designating Vessels of the United States Navy
summary: Standardized naval vessel names: each Navy ship is officially designated by its name preceded only by "United States Ship" or "U.S.S."

title: All Navy vessels to be officially designated by name preceded by "United States Ship" or "U.S.S." and no other words/letters.
Authorizing Appointment of Elza Eugene Phelps as Customs Inspector Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Elza Eugene Phelps to be appointed a customs inspector for confidential duty on merchandise moving over the Tehuantepec National Railway in Mexico, without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Promotion of Marshall M. Pool to Clerk in United States Army Office Without Examination
summary: Permitted Marshall M. Pool to be promoted without examination to a clerical job in the Army purchasing commissary's office at Kansas City, Missouri.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of David Robinson as Immigrant Inspector Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let David Robinson be reinstated as an immigrant inspector, citing his efficiency and familiarity with immigration matters.

title: Certain Hawaii lands at Waimānalo, Oahu, reserved for lighthouse purposes at the Makapuʻu Light Station.
summary: Reserved land at Waimānalo, Oahu, Hawaii, for lighthouse purposes at the Makapuʻu Light Station.

title: Setting Apart the Caribou Forest Reserve, Idaho and Wyoming
summary: Established the Caribou Forest Reserve in Idaho and Wyoming, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Identical to Executive Order 548
summary: Duplicates Executive Order 548, which authorized the Governor of Tutuila to issue certificates of protection to qualifying merchant vessels.

title: Authorizing Issuance of Certificates of Protection by Governor of American Samoa
summary: Empowered the Governor of Tutuila to issue certificates of protection, giving U.S. flag protection to merchant vessels owned by American citizens or by Tutuila and Manua residents who swore allegiance to the United States.

title: Building in Sitka, Alaska, Formerly Used as Governor's Residence Reserved as Naval Hospital
summary: Reserved the building in Sitka, Alaska, formerly the governor's residence, for use as a naval hospital.

title: Addition to the Fort Lincoln Military Reservation, Burleigh County, North Dakota
summary: Added about 32.5 acres in Burleigh County, North Dakota, to the Fort Lincoln Military Reservation, reserving the lots from sale for military purposes.

title: Regulations for Army and Navy General Hospital, Hot Springs, Ark., Amended
summary: Amended the regulations for the Army and Navy General Hospital at Hot Springs, Arkansas.

title: Addition to the Camp John Hay Military Reservation, Luzon, Philippine Islands
summary: Enlarged the Camp John Hay Military Reservation at Baguio, Benguet, on Luzon in the Philippines, to take in additional public lands.

title: Reciprocity with Portugal
summary: Proclaimed an additional agreement with Portugal, concluded November 19, 1902, extending the two nations' 1899 commercial reciprocity agreement to Porto Rico.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Cascade Range Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Expanded the Cascade Range Forest Reserve in Oregon, first proclaimed September 28, 1893, adding more partly timbered lands and reserving them from settlement.

title: Federal Employee Members of Grand Army of the Republic Excused from Duty at Noon, Jan 26, 1907, for Funeral of Russell A. Alger
summary: Excused federal employees who belong to the Grand Army of the Republic from duty at noon on January 26, 1907, to attend the funeral of Russell A. Alger.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Frank P. Nantz as Deputy Collector of Internal Revenue in San Juan, Puerto Rico, Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Frank P. Nantz to be appointed deputy collector of internal revenue at San Juan, Porto Rico, without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James Campbell as Deputy Surveyor of Customs Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let James Campbell, assistant appraiser of merchandise at Baltimore, be appointed deputy surveyor of customs at that port without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Isthmian Canal Commission to Hold the Quarterly Session Scheduled for the First Week in February, 1907, in Washington, D.C., Instead of on the Isthmus of Panama
summary: Moved the Isthmian Canal Commission's February 1907 quarterly session from the Isthmus of Panama to Washington, D.C.

title: Setting Apart the Ouray Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Created the Ouray Forest Reserve in Colorado, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Extending Time Limit for Completion of Work of the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to September 2, 1907
summary: Extended the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission's powers to examine and settle U.S. citizens' claims against Spain until September 2, 1907.

title: Prescribing Rules Governing Peacetime Purchase of Discharge from the Marine Corps
summary: Set rules letting Marine Corps enlisted men in their first enlistment buy their discharge in peacetime after one year, at $120, $100 or $90 depending on service, with relief for men supporting destitute relatives.

title: Setting Apart the Monticello Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Established the Monticello Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Stony Creek Forest Reserve, California
summary: Set apart the Stony Creek Forest Reserve in California, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Glenwood Forest Reserve, Utah
summary: Created the Glenwood Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Big Burros Forest Reserve, New Mexico
summary: Established the Big Burros Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Norman Oswell Cully as Messenger at Naval Academy Without Examination
summary: Allowed Norman Oswell Cully to be appointed messenger to the superintendent of the Naval Academy without a civil-service examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Elizabeth M. Leech as Clerk Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted Elizabeth M. Leech to be appointed to a clerical position in the classified civil service without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Reserving Viti Rocks, or Islands, in Bellingham Bay, Washington, for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Reserved the Viti Rocks, or islands, in Bellingham Bay, Washington, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mrs. George H. Hildreth as Clerk in Bureau of Pensions Without Examination
summary: Let Mrs. George H. Hildreth be appointed to a clerical position in the Bureau of Pensions without examination.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the San Jacinto Forest Reserve, California
summary: Enlarged the San Jacinto Forest Reserve, first proclaimed February 22, 1897, by adding partly timbered lands in California and reserving them from settlement.

title: Excluding Lands from the Little Belt Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Cut lands out of the Little Belt Forest Reserve in Montana and restored them to the public domain.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mazie R. Fountaine as Clerk in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mazie R. Fountaine, a former Smithsonian Institution clerk, to be reinstated as a Treasury Department clerk without meeting civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Mrs. George H. Hildreth as Clerk in Classified Service Without Examination
summary: Broadened Mrs. George H. Hildreth's exemption so she may take any clerical position in the classified service without examination, revoking the February 13 order limited to the Bureau of Pensions.

title: Authorizing Appointment of W. H. Teepe as Clerk in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Cleared W. H. Teepe, a tabulator on the Post Office Department's mail-weighing work, for a permanent clerical job in the Department without the usual civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Robert L. Slagle as Clerk in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Robert L. Slagle, an assistant messenger in the Post Office Department, move up to a permanent clerical position there without the usual civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of James H. Adams in Classified Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed James H. Adams, who served in the Treasury Department's classified service from 1892 to 1904, to be reinstated without regard to the civil-service rules.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Big Belt Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Redrew the Big Belt Forest Reserve in Montana, adding timbered lands and cutting out others, which were restored and opened to settlement.

title: Establishing Imnaha Forest Reserve, Oregon, in Place of the Wallowa and Chesnimnus Forest Reserves
summary: Combined Oregon's Wallowa and Chesnimnus forest reserves, plus added lands, into one new reserve: the Imnaha Forest Reserve.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Park Range Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Changed the boundaries of the Park Range Forest Reserve in Colorado, adding timbered lands and excluding others, which were opened to settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Holy Cross Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Enlarged the Holy Cross Forest Reserve in Colorado with additional lands partly covered with timber.

title: Establishing the Bear Lodge Forest Reserve, Wyoming
summary: Established the Bear Lodge Forest Reserve in Wyoming, setting apart timbered public lands and reserving them from settlement.

title: Establishing the Colville Forest Reserve, Washington
summary: Established the Colville Forest Reserve in Washington on timbered public lands, with margin notes addressing allotments to Indians.

title: Establishing the Las Animas Forest Reserve, Colorado and New Mexico
summary: Created the Las Animas Forest Reserve on timbered public lands spanning Colorado and the Territory of New Mexico.

title: Amending Regulations for the Army and Navy General Hospital, Hot Springs, Arkansas, Regarding Rations and Subsistence
summary: Rewrote ration rules at the Army and Navy General Hospital in Hot Springs, Arkansas, paying 30 cents per ration for soldiers, nurses, sailors and Marines instead of issuing food in kind.

title: Establishing the Little Rockies Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Established the Little Rockies Forest Reserve in Montana, setting apart public lands partly covered with timber.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho
summary: Redrew the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, adding timbered lands in Wyoming, Montana and Idaho and excluding others, which were opened to settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Port Neuf Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Set apart the Port Neuf Forest Reserve in Idaho on public lands partly covered with timber.

title: Setting Apart the Palouse Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Set apart the Palouse Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Weiser Forest Reserve, Idaho
summary: Adjusted the Weiser Forest Reserve in Idaho again, adding timbered lands and excluding others, which were reopened to settlement.

title: Setting Apart the Cabinet Forest Reserve, Montana and Idaho
summary: Set apart the Cabinet Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in Montana and Idaho.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Rainier Forest Reserve, Washington
summary: Enlarged the Mt. Rainier Forest Reserve in Washington with more timbered land and, per the margin notes, changed its name to the Rainier Forest Reserve.

title: Modifying Boundaries of the Washington Forest Reserve, Washington
summary: Modified the Washington Forest Reserve, excluding some lands and adding new timbered tracts in Washington; excluded lands were opened to settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Ashland Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Further enlarged the Ashland Forest Reserve in Oregon with additional lands partly covered with timber.

title: Setting Apart the Coquille Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Set apart the Coquille Forest Reserve in Oregon on public lands partly covered with timber.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Cascade Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Added more timbered Oregon land to the Cascade Forest Reserve, first created in 1893 as the Cascade Range Forest Reserve.

title: Setting Apart the Umpqua Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Set apart the Umpqua Forest Reserve in Oregon, reserving timbered public lands from settlement.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve, Oregon, and Incorporating Therewith the Maury Mountain Forest Reserve
summary: Folded Oregon's Maury Mountain Forest Reserve into the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve and enlarged the combined reserve with additional lands.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve, Colorado and Wyoming
summary: Further enlarged the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve with timbered lands in Colorado and Wyoming.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Lewis and Clark Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Added more timbered Montana land to the Lewis and Clark Forest Reserve, established in 1897.

title: Setting Apart the Otter Forest Reserve, Montana
summary: Set apart the Otter Forest Reserve in Montana on public lands partly covered with timber.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Olympic Forest Reserve, Washington
summary: Further enlarged the Olympic Forest Reserve in Washington with additional lands partly covered with timber.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Montezuma Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Enlarged the Montezuma Forest Reserve in Colorado with additional timbered lands.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the San Juan Forest Reserve, Colorado
summary: Enlarged the San Juan Forest Reserve in Colorado, created in 1905, with more lands partly covered with timber.

title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Priest River Forest Reserve, Idaho and Washington
summary: Further enlarged the Priest River Forest Reserve with timbered lands in Idaho and Washington.

title: Setting Apart the Tillamook Forest Reserve, Oregon
summary: Set apart the Tillamook Forest Reserve in Oregon on public lands partly covered with timber.

title: Lands at Cape Spencer, Alaska, Reserved for Lighthouse Purposes
summary: Reserved the southern tip of the Cape Spencer headland at the entrance to Cross Sound, Alaska, with nearby islands and land around Dick's Arm, for lighthouse purposes.

title: Coal Land Withdrawals Included by Proclamation Within Forest Reserves Not to be Excluded from Operation of Said Proclamation
summary: Directed that coal-land withdrawals included within forest reserves by proclamation are not to be excluded from the operation of those proclamations.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Lillie L. Wright as Clerk in Patent Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Lillie L. Wright, a former Patent Office clerk, to be reinstated no matter how long she had been out of the service.

title: Appointing John F. Stevens as Chairman and George W. Goethals as Members of Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Named John F. Stevens chairman of the Isthmian Canal Commission and George W. Goethals a member.

title: Authorizing Appointment of George W. Pitts as Clerk in Treasury Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed George W. Pitts to be appointed a Treasury Department clerk without meeting the civil-service rules.

title: Forbidding Publication of Law Opinions by Subordinates in Dept of Justice Without Approval of Attorney General
summary: Barred subordinates in the Department of Justice from publishing legal opinions without the Attorney General's approval.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James G. Massey as Clerk in Department of the Interior Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let James G. Massey be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of the Interior without reference to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of John C. Eversman, Sr. to Competitive Position in Pension Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed John C. Eversman, Sr., a special examiner in the Pension Office, to be appointed or transferred to a competitive position there.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement and Transfer of P. J. Hughes to Clerk in War Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let P. J. Hughes, who left the Isthmian Canal service because of ill health, be reinstated and transferred as a clerk to the War Department.

title: Authorizing Appointment of C. F. House as Clerk in Naval Training Station, North Chicago, Illinois, Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed C. F. House to be hired as a $1,000-a-year clerk at the Great Lakes Naval Training Station in North Chicago, Illinois, without civil-service rules.

title: Setting Aside Chaco Canyon National Monument, New Mexico
summary: Proclaimed Chaco Canyon National Monument in New Mexico, protecting its prehistoric pueblo ruins and burial grounds, described as being of extraordinary interest for their number, size and relics.

title: Designating F. C. Ainsworth and J. Franklin Bell as Acting Sec'y of War
summary: Designated F. C. Ainsworth and J. Franklin Bell to serve as Acting Secretary of War.

title: Regulations for executing and recording deeds in the Canal Zone (eff. Apr. 15, 1907) promulgated.
summary: Issued regulations for executing and recording deeds in the Canal Zone, effective April 15, 1907.

title: Dividing Canal Zone in Panama into Four Administrative Districts, and Reorganizing Municipal Offices Within
summary: Split the Canal Zone into four administrative districts (Ancon, Emperador, Gorgona and Cristobal), each with a tax collector taking over municipal treasury and assessment duties.

title: Amending Penal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure of the Canal Zone Regarding Punishments
summary: Amended the Canal Zone's Penal Code, revising punishments for assault, battery, failure to support a wife or child, grand larceny and embezzlement of public funds.

title: Authorizing Ministers and Judges to Perform Marriage Ceremonies in Canal Zone
summary: Allowed ministers in regular standing, judges of courts of record and municipal or district judges to perform marriages in the Canal Zone.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Classification of Employees in New Free-Delivery Post Offices
summary: Changed civil-service Rule II so post offices newly given free delivery come under the rules, but staff appointed within 60 days of the change aren't classified without Commission consent.

title: Regulating the Entrance of Japanese or Korean Laborers into U.S. Territories
summary: Barred Japanese and Korean laborers holding passports to Mexico, Canada or Hawaii from entering the continental United States from those places, and told the Secretary of Commerce and Labor to enforce it.

title: Authorizing Appointment of R. H. Mitchell as Watchman in Department of the Interior Without Examination
summary: Allowed R. H. Mitchell to be appointed a watchman in the Department of the Interior without examination.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Dr. A. Brown in Department of Agriculture Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Dr. A. Brown join the Department of Agriculture without examination, citing his special ability for work under the pure-food and drugs law.

title: Portions of Great Falls Land District, Montana, Transferred to Glasgow Land District
summary: Moved parts of the Great Falls land district in Montana into the Glasgow land district.

title: Revoking Establishment of Portales National Forest, New Mexico
summary: Revoked the Portales National Forest in New Mexico, no longer needed for experimental forest purposes, and returned its lands to the public domain, open to settlement.

title: Appointing New Members of the Isthmian Canal Commission and Fixing their Compensation
summary: Appointed Maj. William L. Sibert, Maj. David Du B. Gaillard and Civil Engineer Harry H. Rousseau to the Isthmian Canal Commission at $14,000 a year, replacing three members who resigned.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Charles P. Galpin as Clerk in Pension Office Without Examination
summary: Allowed Charles P. Galpin, a Pension Office messenger, to be appointed to a clerical position there without examination.

title: Amending Executive Order No. 577½ of March 4, 1907, Prescribing Additional Compensation for Isthmian Canal Commissioner George W. Goethals
summary: Amended the March 4 order to give Isthmian Canal Commissioner George W. Goethals a furnished house on the Isthmus and expenses for official travel away from it.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Frederick M. Kerby as Clerk in Department of the Interior Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Frederick M. Kerby be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of the Interior without reference to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Harlan Updegraff as Alaskan Assistant in Bureau of Education Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Permitted Harlan Updegraff to be appointed Alaskan assistant in the Bureau of Education without reference to civil-service rules.

title: Code of Civil Procedure for the Canal Zone promulgated.
summary: Put a Code of Civil Procedure into effect for the Canal Zone.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Mahlon Pursel as Clerk in War Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed Mahlon Pursel to be reinstated as a clerk in the War Department's Adjutant-General's Office despite the civil-service time limit on reinstatement.

title: Authorizing Reinstatement of F. T. Quinlan as Inspector of Furs in Quartermaster's Department in Philadelphia Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed F. T. Quinlan to be reinstated as an inspector of furs in the quartermaster's department at Philadelphia.

title: Authorizing Transfer of W. P. Armstrong, Law Clerk in Isthmian Canal Commission, Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let W. P. Armstrong, a law clerk with the Isthmian Canal Commission, transfer to another competitive position paying up to $2,500 a year, waiving transfer-rule limits.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Theresa S. Aubright as Clerk in Classified Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed Theresa S. Aubright to be appointed to a clerical position in the classified civil service without examination.

title: Call for Election of Delegates in Philippine Island
summary: Called the general election of delegates to the Philippine Assembly, the popular assembly that would share legislative power with the Philippine Commission under the 1902 act of Congress.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Private Secretary to Commissioner of the General Land Office Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed one clerk or examiner to be appointed as private secretary to the Commissioner of the General Land Office without reference to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James Bronson Reynolds as Chinese Inspector in Immigration Service Without Examination
summary: Allowed James Bronson Reynolds to be appointed a Chinese inspector in the Immigration Service without civil-service examination.

title: Enlarging Grande Island Military Reservation, Luzon, Philippine Islands
summary: Enlarged the Grande Island military reservation off Luzon in the Philippines to take in all rocks, shoals and islands within one mile of the island's low-water line.

title: Appointing George W. Goethals, U.S. Army, as Chairman of Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Made Lt. Col. George W. Goethals chairman of the Isthmian Canal Commission, succeeding John F. Stevens, who resigned.

title: Appointing Joseph C. S. Blackburn as Member of the Isthmian Canal Commission
summary: Appointed Joseph C. S. Blackburn to the Isthmian Canal Commission at $14,000 a year, with a furnished house on the Isthmus and travel expenses.

title: Authorizing Transfer of Jake T. Patrick to Competitive Position in Internal Revenue Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Jake T. Patrick, a storekeeper-gauger in Kentucky's eighth internal-revenue district, transfer to a competitive position in that district.

title: Ordering Four Hour Workdays on Saturdays During Summer for Certain War Department Employees
summary: Made four hours a full Saturday's work in July, August and September for civilian mechanics, laborers and other employees at War Department arsenals, depots and Army headquarters offices.

title: Enlarging Big Burros National Forest, New Mexico
summary: Enlarged the Big Burros National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico with additional lands partly covered with timber.

title: Amending Instructions to Diplomatic Officers and Consular Regulations Relating to Expatriation, Citizenship, Naturalization, and Passports
summary: Rewrote diplomatic and consular rules on citizenship and passports, covering children of citizens born abroad, wives of citizens, and American women who marry foreigners.

title: Amending Consular Regulations, Paragraph 172, Regarding Registration of American Citizens Abroad
summary: Updated consular regulations so consulates keep, and publicize, a register of American citizens living in their districts.

title: Redefining Boundaries of Camp Downes Military Reservation, Ormoc, Leyte, Philippine Islands
summary: Corrected the boundaries of the Camp Downes military reservation at Ormoc, Leyte, in the Philippines after a survey found the original metes and bounds were wrong.

title: Spanish War Veterans in District of Columbia Excused from Duty Apr. 12 for Unveiling of Rough Riders Monument at Arlington
summary: Excused Spanish War veterans in the District of Columbia from duty on April 12 so they could attend the unveiling of the Rough Riders Monument at Arlington.

title: Authorizing Promotion of John H. McTeer to Clerk in Treasury Department After Examination Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Allowed John H. McTeer, a skilled laborer in the Treasury Department, to be promoted to clerk after passing the exam before completing two years in a subclerical grade.

title: Setting Apart Toquima National Forest, Nevada
summary: Set apart the Toquima National Forest in Nevada on public lands partly covered with timber, "for the use and benefit of the people."

title: Enlarging Gallinas National Forest, New Mexico
summary: Enlarged the Gallinas National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico with additional timbered lands.

title: Setting Apart Monitor National Forest, Nevada
summary: Set apart the Monitor National Forest in Nevada, reserving timbered public lands from settlement or entry.

title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Limitations on Transfer
summary: Rewrote the civil-service transfer rule: transfers require six months' classified service, and moves between Washington departments or independent offices require three years, which the Commission may waive.

title: Gunnison Land District, Colorado, Abolished; Transferred to Montrose Land District
summary: Abolished the Gunnison land district in Colorado and transferred its business to the Montrose land district.

title: Setting Apart Guadalupe National Forest, New Mexico
summary: Created the Guadalupe National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico on public lands partly covered with timber.

title: Enlarging Stony Creek National Forest, California
summary: Added more partly timbered land in California to the Stony Creek National Forest and redrew its boundaries.

title: Amending Consular Service Regulation of June 27, 1906, Governing Appointment and Promotion in the Consular Service
summary: Rewrote a section of the 1906 consular service order so consular clerks, vice consuls, interpreters and similar officers appointed by examination could be promoted on ability and efficiency.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Charles L. Murphy as Skilled Laborer in Bureau of Fisheries Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Charles L. Murphy be permanently appointed a skilled laborer at the Bureau of Fisheries' central station, since no other eligibles had his qualifications.

title: Modifying Lincoln National Forest, New Mexico
summary: Redrew the Lincoln National Forest in New Mexico Territory, adding some partly timbered lands and cutting others out.

title: Setting Apart Sacramento National Forest, New Mexico
summary: Created the Sacramento National Forest from partly timbered public lands in New Mexico Territory, including part of the area once in the Lincoln National Forest.

title: Enlarging Beaver National Forest, Utah
summary: Enlarged the Beaver National Forest in Utah with additional lands partly covered with timber.

title: Enlarging Manti National Forest, Utah
summary: Expanded Utah's Manti National Forest to take in more partly timbered land.

title: Excusing Members of Certain Civil War Societies in Washington from Work for Unveiling of George McClellan Statue
summary: Excused federal workers in Washington who belonged to Civil War veterans' societies from duty on May 2, 1907, so they could attend the unveiling of the Gen. George B. McClellan statue.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Frederick L. Dunlap as Associate Chemist in Department of Agriculture Without Examination
summary: Allowed Frederick L. Dunlap of Michigan to be appointed associate chemist and member of the food and drug inspection in the Department of Agriculture without examination.

title: Appointing Huntington Wilson as acting Secretary of State
summary: Named Huntington Wilson acting Secretary of State.

title: Enlarging Fish Lake National Forest, Utah
summary: Added partly timbered lands in Utah to the Fish Lake National Forest.

title: Authorizing Permanent Appointment of Harrison L. Deam as Watchman in Department of the Interior Without Regard to Civil Service Rules
summary: Let Civil War veteran Harrison L. Deam, a temporary watchman at the Interior Department, be appointed permanently without regard to civil-service rules.

title: Authorizing Appointment of James D. Rowan, Jr. and Charles L. Gooch as Gardeners and William Grant as Laboratory Helper in Department of Agriculture After Examination
summary: Allowed three Agriculture Department student assistants to be appointed after noncompetitive exams: James D. Rowan Jr. and Charles L. Gooch as gardeners, and William Grant as a laboratory helper.

title: Authorizing Appointment of Elsie E. Lower as Clerk and Artist in Department of Agriculture Without Examination
summary: Allowed Elsie E. Lower of Pennsylvania, an Agriculture Department student assistant, to be appointed clerk and artist without examination.
